red-toadstools.toadstools with white spots: Paint the caps deep red, wash and drybrush them pink red, then dot a few pale spots on the caps.
red-toadstools.paint fly agaric mushrooms: Base white stems and deep red caps, wash dark brown, drybrush bright pink red then pale pink, and add pale spots if you like.
red-toadstools.tiny mushrooms for forest base: Glue them in a small cluster of mixed sizes, in shade by a rock, root or tuft, then tuck moss round the stems.
red-toadstools.how to paint red caps and pale stems: Paint the stems white and caps deep red, keeping them apart, wash dark brown with two coats on the stems, then drybrush the caps pink.
red-toadstools.fungus on bases: Glue small toadstools in a mixed cluster in shade, paint white stems and deep red caps, wash brown and drybrush the caps pink.
red-toadstools.mushroom cluster by a tree root: Glue a cluster of mixed sizes in the shade of the root, then tuck moss or small tufts round the stems.
red-toadstools.fairy toadstool colours: Deep red caps drybrushed bright pink red and pale pink, on white stems toned down with a dark brown wash, with pale spots if you like.
red-toadstools.woodland base mushrooms: Cluster toadstools in shade by a rock or root, paint them red and white, wash brown, drybrush the caps, and add moss around them.
red-toadstools.paint mushroom caps: Base the caps deep red, wash dark brown, drybrush bright pink red all over, then a gentle pass of pale pink on top.

snowy-flagstones.snow on flagstones base: Paint the flagstones grey and edge them, then spoon snow paste into drifts and touch thin blue into the wet snow for cold shadow.
snowy-flagstones.winter base with paving stones: Paint grey flagstones with green tints and dead leaves, then spoon snow paste into drifts with a thin blue shadow touched in while wet.
snowy-flagstones.how to paint snow with blue shadows: While the snow paste is still wet, touch in a very thin blue so it soaks in as cold shadow.
snowy-flagstones.snowy base for display model: Test fit the model, paint the flagstones and details, add snow drifts with blue shadows, then glue the model on and paint the rim black.
snowy-flagstones.flagstones with dead leaves: Paint the stones, then pick out the leaves and small details before you add the snow.
snowy-flagstones.grey stone tiles with snow: Base brown grey, overbrush warm mid grey with a thin black wash, edge light grey, then spoon in snow drifts.
snowy-flagstones.make snow look cold not white: Drop a very thin cold blue into the snow paste while it is wet so it soaks in as shadow.
snowy-flagstones.paint the base before gluing the model: Paint the base fully first, and only glue the model on once the snow is completely dry.
snowy-flagstones.icy paved courtyard base: Grey flagstones with light grey edges, snow paste spooned into drifts and a thin cold blue dropped into the wet snow.
snowy-flagstones.how do i paint flagstone bases: Base brown grey, overbrush warm mid grey, thin black wash, light grey edges and scratches, then thin deep green glazes on random stones.

weathered-marble.old marble floor base: Prime black, dust grey, drybrush deep ivory, wash brown and green on the soil, then bring the ivory back and dust pale bone over it.
weathered-marble.how to paint marble quickly: Prime black, dust grey from above, then drybrush deep ivory in circles, leaving grey in the recesses.
weathered-marble.ancient temple floor: Drybrush deep ivory over black and grey primer, wash brown and green for age, then drybrush warm ivory and pale bone.
weathered-marble.worn stone tiles with moss: Wash brown and green together on the base for age and a hint of moss, and let it dry fully before the next drybrush.
weathered-marble.ivory stone base: Drybrush the stone deep ivory over a grey primer, wash it mossy brown, then dust warm ivory and pale bone back over.
weathered-marble.cracked marble paving: See: drybrushed old marble flooring with dirt and moss, in this entry's steps.
weathered-marble.quick stone flooring paint: Prime black, dust grey, then drybrush deep ivory, warm ivory and pale bone, with a brown and green wash between.
weathered-marble.marble base looks too clean: Wash brown and green at once over it for dirt and age, then bring the ivory back with a lighter drybrush.
weathered-marble.ruined palace floor: See: quick weathered stone flooring with dirt and moss, built up by drybrushing ivory over grey.
weathered-marble.drybrushed marble: Heavy deep ivory over black and grey primer, a mossy brown wash, then lighter warm ivory and a pale bone dusting.

beaks-and-talons.how to paint a beak: Base it yellow orange, streak pale cream along it, glaze near black back from the tip, and put light grey on the very tip.
beaks-and-talons.bird claws: Yellow orange base, pale cream on the knuckles, near black glazes fading from the tips, and a light grey line on top of each claw.
beaks-and-talons.eagle talons: Base yellow orange, glaze near black from the tips back so they fade dark, then a fine light grey line along the top of each claw.
beaks-and-talons.yellow beak with dark tip: Thin yellow orange coats, cream streaks, then thin near black glazes from the tip back, each stopping shorter.
beaks-and-talons.griffon beak and feet: Yellow orange beak and feet, pale cream streaks, near black fading in from the tips, and light grey on the claw edges and beak tip.
beaks-and-talons.bird feet colour: A yellow orange base, with pale cream on raised scales and knuckles and claws that fade to near black.
beaks-and-talons.paint claws fading to black: Glaze thin near black from the tips back, each coat stopping shorter, so the claws fade dark.
beaks-and-talons.hawk beak recipe: Yellow orange base, pale cream streaks, near black glazes from the tip back, and light grey on the very tip.
beaks-and-talons.scaly bird legs: Base yellow orange, then pick out the raised scales and knuckles with small touches of pale cream.
beaks-and-talons.owl beak and talons: Yellow orange base, pale cream streaks, glazed near black at the tips, with fine light grey on claw edges and beak tip.

blue-black-armour.blue black armor: Black base, then stacked edge highlights of very dark blue grey, mid blue grey, and pale icy blue on the sharpest edges.
blue-black-armour.black armour with blue highlights: Paint it black, then edge in very dark blue grey, a thinner mid blue grey inside that, and pale icy blue dots on the corners.
blue-black-armour.how do i highlight black armour blue: Stack edge lines: a fairly thick very dark blue grey, a thinner mid blue grey inside it, and pale icy blue only on the sharpest edges.
blue-black-armour.edge highlight black panels: Run a fairly thick very dark blue grey line on every edge and panel break, then thinner, lighter lines inside it.
blue-black-armour.dark armour that still shows detail: Edge highlight in stacked blue greys so the detail shows, keeping the palest blue to the sharpest edges so it still reads black.
blue-black-armour.cold black power armour: Black base with very dark blue grey, mid blue grey and pale icy blue edge highlights stacked inside each other.
blue-black-armour.corner dots on armour edges: Put pale icy blue dots on the corners and sharpest lit edges only; overdo it and the armour stops reading black.
blue-black-armour.black armor looks like a blob: Lift it with stacked edge highlights in blue greys on every edge and panel break, from very dark to pale icy blue.
blue-black-armour.blue grey edge highlights: Start with a fairly thick very dark blue grey line, then a thinner mid blue grey inside it, then pale icy blue on the sharpest edges.
blue-black-armour.midnight black armour recipe: Black, then edges of very dark blue grey, mid blue grey and pale icy blue, finishing with corner dots.

bright-green-skin.bright green skin: Yellow green one coat paint over a pale cream undercoat, pale stony grey on the raised areas, a second yellow green coat, then warm tan touches.
bright-green-skin.how to paint green monster skin fast: Paint a yellow green one coat paint over a pale cream undercoat, pick out the raised areas in pale grey, then give it a second coat.
bright-green-skin.goblin skin green: A yellow green one coat paint over pale cream, stony grey highlights blended with a second coat, and tiny warm tan touches.
bright-green-skin.one coat green skin: Use a yellow green one coat paint over a pale cream undercoat, soaking up any pools with a dry brush.
bright-green-skin.vivid green orc skin: Yellow green one coat paint over a pale undercoat, pale stony grey on the muscles, then a second coat to blend it into a gradient.
bright-green-skin.green skin looks flat: Pick out the cheeks, brow, nose, knuckles and muscle edges in pale stony grey, then glaze yellow green back over to blend them.
bright-green-skin.punchy green skin with contrast: Over pale cream, coat it yellow green, highlight in pale stony grey, and a second yellow green coat turns the light areas into a gradient.
bright-green-skin.green skin over white undercoat: Use a pale cream undercoat rather than white, then the yellow green one coat paint over it, soaking up any pools.
bright-green-skin.troll skin bright green: Yellow green one coat over pale cream, stony grey on the raised muscles, a second yellow green coat, and warm tan touches on face and hands.
bright-green-skin.make green skin pop: Add tiny warm tan touches on the face and hands; it makes the skin look alive.

cold-desaturated-skin.pale grim skin: Mid flesh base, a thinned pinkish brown wash in the creases, then highlights of flesh mixed with a little pale blue or violet.
cold-desaturated-skin.cold skin tones: Mix a little pale blue or violet into the flesh for the highlights, finishing in pale violet grey on the lit side.
cold-desaturated-skin.vampire skin: Mid flesh, a pinkish brown wash, greyed flesh cooled with pale blue or violet, then pale violet grey edges on the lit side.
cold-desaturated-skin.sickly pale face: Base mid flesh, wash the sockets and creases pinkish brown, then highlight with flesh cooled by a little pale blue or violet.
cold-desaturated-skin.blue tinted skin highlights: Mix a little pale blue or violet into the flesh for highlights, and add white once it starts to look blue.
cold-desaturated-skin.gaunt dead looking skin: See: grim, cold living skin, made by cooling the highlights with pale blue or violet.
cold-desaturated-skin.desaturated flesh: Mix pale blue or violet into the flesh for greyed, cold highlights, finishing in pale violet grey.
cold-desaturated-skin.ghostly skin colour: See: grim, shadowy skin cooled to pale violet grey, which can be pushed paler for a ghostly look.
cold-desaturated-skin.skin for a grimdark character: Mid flesh with a pinkish brown wash in the creases, then cold highlights of flesh with pale blue or violet mixed in.
cold-desaturated-skin.cool violet skin highlights: Mix a little violet into the flesh for highlights, finish in pale violet grey on the lit side, and add white once it looks blue.

deep-red-cloth.deep red cloak: Base deep wine red over black, then drybrush mid cherry red, light pinkish red and a very soft pale bone on top edges.
deep-red-cloth.how to paint red robes: Several thin coats of deep wine red over black, then build up drybrushes of cherry red, pinkish red and a soft pale bone.
deep-red-cloth.rich red cloth with drybrushing: Base deep wine red, drybrush slowly up through mid cherry red and light pinkish red, mixing each with the last to avoid jumps.
deep-red-cloth.red cloak over black primer: Use several thin coats of deep wine red over black, keeping the recesses dark, then drybrush up through lighter reds.
deep-red-cloth.dark red fabric recipe: Deep wine red base, then drybrushes of mid cherry red, light pinkish red and soft pale bone on top edges.
deep-red-cloth.crimson cape: Deep wine red base, then drybrushed mid cherry red, light pinkish red and a touch of pale bone on the top edges.
deep-red-cloth.red cloth looks pink: Mix each lighter red with the last colour to avoid a big jump, and keep the pale bone very soft and to the top edges only.
deep-red-cloth.cool red robes: Use a deep wine red base and a mid cherry red, which give a rich cool red, built up slowly by drybrushing.
deep-red-cloth.drybrush cloth red: Start with a mix of wine red and cherry red, then pure cherry, then red with a little white, building up slowly.
deep-red-cloth.blood red cloak: Deep wine red over black, drybrushed up through mid cherry red and light pinkish red, keeping the recesses dark.

glowing-fungus.glowing mushrooms: Paint the surroundings dark green, the tips white, glaze cyan from the base up, then add white with gloss varnish on the tip.
glowing-fungus.cyan glow: Cover the glowing part in white, glaze thin cyan from the base up, and keep the very tip the palest part.
glowing-fungus.how to make fungus glow: Paint the tips pure white over dark surroundings, glaze cyan from the base up, and add glossy white on the tip.
glowing-fungus.bioluminescent mushrooms: White tips glazed cyan from the base up, with the very tip palest, over dark matt green surroundings.
glowing-fungus.glowing toadstools on a base: Keep the base dark and flat with dark green and a little black, then white tips glazed cyan from the base up.
glowing-fungus.bright blue glow on a dark base: Make the surroundings dark green with a little matt black, then white glazed thinly with cyan on the glowing parts.
glowing-fungus.cave mushrooms that light up: White tips glazed cyan from the base up, the very tip palest, with glossy white on top to look brighter.
glowing-fungus.make something look like it gives off li: Keep the surroundings dark and flat, make the source white with thin colour glazed from the base up, and leave the tip palest.
glowing-fungus.fungus glow effect: White over dark green surroundings, thin cyan glazed from the base up, and white mixed with gloss varnish on the tip.
glowing-fungus.neon mushrooms: Paint the tips white, glaze cyan from the base up leaving the tip palest, then add white mixed with gloss varnish.

green-water-stains.verdigris streaks: Glaze thin deep sea green where there is no rust and let it run down, then stipple turquoise and pale mint around the rivets.
green-water-stains.green stains on metal: Dab thin deep sea green so it pools and runs down, then stipple bright turquoise inside it and pale mint at the rivets.
green-water-stains.water stains on armour: Let thin deep sea green pool and run down the metal, then stipple bright turquoise and pale mint around rivets and scratches.
green-water-stains.green corrosion drips: Dab thin deep sea green and let it run down, then stipple bright turquoise inside it around rivets and scratches.
green-water-stains.verdigris and rust together: Put the green stains where there is no rust, so the cool green sits against the rust on dulled metal.
green-water-stains.weathered bronze streaks: See: cool green verdigris stains on dulled metal, in this entry's steps.
green-water-stains.green run off under rivets: Dab thin deep sea green near rivets and let it run down, then stipple turquoise and tiny touches of pale mint around the rivets.
green-water-stains.green patina streaks: Deep sea green glazed to pool and run, bright turquoise stippled inside it, then tiny pale mint touches round the rivets.
green-water-stains.algae stains on metal: See: green stains on dulled metal from thin deep sea green, turquoise and pale mint.
green-water-stains.streaky green weathering: Glaze thin deep sea green and let it pool and run down, then stipple turquoise and pale mint inside the first green.

heavy-rust.heavy rust: Layer dark red oxide where water sits, sponge rust brown inside it, stipple orange smaller again, then drybrush dark steel on the edges.
heavy-rust.how do i paint really rusty metal: Dark red oxide where water would sit, sponged rust brown, stippled orange hotspots, then dark steel on edges so bare metal shows.
heavy-rust.rust with a sponge: Dab smaller rust brown patches inside the dark red oxide with an almost dry sponge, then stipple orange smaller again.
heavy-rust.rusty metal: Build it in shrinking patches, from dark red oxide to rust brown to bright orange, heaviest where water pools.
heavy-rust.layered rust effect: Dark red oxide, then sponged rust brown, stippled orange inside that, and a dark steel drybrush on the sharp edges.
heavy-rust.rust looks fake and orange: Build it up from dark red oxide, keep the bright orange to small hotspots where water sits, and let bare steel show on the edges.
heavy-rust.pitted rusty armour: Paint gritty texture paint first for pitting, then dark red oxide, sponged rust brown and stippled orange.
heavy-rust.where to put rust on a vehicle: Put it where water would sit or pool, with the brightest orange hotspots there.
heavy-rust.old corroded tank hull: Dark red oxide where water pools, gritty texture for pitting, sponged rust brown and orange, then dark steel on sharp edges.
heavy-rust.rusty scrap metal: Layer dark red oxide, sponge rust brown, stipple orange, and give the sharp edges a light dark steel drybrush.

ochre-armour.ochre armour: Base light ochre, glaze orange brown into panel lines, drop dark warm brown in, then edge pale flesh, pale cream and white dots.
ochre-armour.sandy yellow armour: Light ochre base with an orange brown glaze and dark warm brown in the panel lines, then pale cream edges.
ochre-armour.how do i paint mustard yellow tanks: Light ochre base, orange brown glaze on lower panels, dark warm brown in the panel lines, and pale cream edges.
ochre-armour.desert yellow vehicle: Base light ochre, glaze orange brown into the panel lines and lower panels, then shade and edge in pale cream.
ochre-armour.yellow ochre panels: Light ochre base, orange brown glazed into the panel lines, a dark warm brown shade, and chunky pale edges.
ochre-armour.khaki armour: See: a warm sandy ochre armour built from light ochre with orange brown glazes and pale cream edges.
ochre-armour.dusty yellow armour: Light ochre base, orange brown glaze on lower panels, dark warm brown shade, then pale flesh, pale cream and white edges.
ochre-armour.yellow that covers over black: A light ochre base covers fairly well by brush, even over black.
ochre-armour.tan vehicle colour: See: a warm sandy ochre for vehicles, glazed orange brown and edged pale cream.
ochre-armour.ochre tank: Light ochre base, orange brown glaze and dark warm brown in the panel lines, then a chunky pale flesh edge and fine pale cream.

painted-steel.steel without metallic paint: Prime black, base dark blue black, layer mid blue grey where light catches, then tiny near white dots on the sharpest points.
painted-steel.non metallic steel: Black prime, dark blue black base, a big jump to mid blue grey where light catches, then near white dots on the sharpest points.
painted-steel.nmm silver: Dark blue black over black, a mid blue grey where the light catches, then near white dots, all without metallic paint.
painted-steel.painted metal blue steel: Black prime, a dark blue black base leaving the deepest shadow black, mid blue grey reflections, and near white dots.
painted-steel.how to paint metal without metallics: Look at the model under a lamp to see where reflections fall, then paint them from blue black up to near white.
painted-steel.fake metal with normal paint: Paint dark blue black, then a big jump to mid blue grey where light catches, glazed to smooth, with near white dots on top.
painted-steel.nmm armour: Black, dark blue black, mid blue grey only where light catches, glazed smooth, then near white with pale yellow as tiny dots.
painted-steel.blue grey steel effect: Black with a muted blue for the base, mid blue grey reflections glazed smooth, then near white dots.
painted-steel.non metallic metal for beginners: Check reflections under a lamp, then paint dark blue black, mid blue grey where light catches, and near white dots.
painted-steel.steel using black and white: Build it from black and dark blue black up to a mid blue grey, finishing with white and a touch of pale yellow as tiny dots.

pitted-green-armour.pitted green armour: Cool blue green base with a dark green wash, stipple dark green blobs and warm yellow green dabs, then warm brown into the pits.
pitted-green-armour.rotten green armor: Base cool blue green, stipple random dark green blobs heavier low down, then warm brown in the panel lines and pits.
pitted-green-armour.how do i paint corroded green armour: Stipple dark green blobs over a cool blue green base, dab yellow green on highlights, and wash warm brown into the pits.
pitted-green-armour.mottled texture on armour: Stipple random dark green blobs, heavier low down, then smaller controlled dabs of warm yellow green on the highlight areas.
pitted-green-armour.diseased armour with brown pits: Mottle cool blue green armour by stippling, then run a warm brown wash into the panel lines and pits.
pitted-green-armour.plague armour look: See: a mottled, pitted blue green armour with warm brown pits, in this entry's steps.
pitted-green-armour.blue green armour recipe: Several thin coats of cool blue green, a dark green wash, stippled dark green and warm yellow green, then pale khaki edges.
pitted-green-armour.weathered green power armour: Stipple dark green low down, black in the deepest areas, yellow green on highlights, warm brown in the pits and pale khaki on top edges.
pitted-green-armour.filthy pitted metal: Stipple dark and yellow green over a blue green base, wash warm brown into panel lines and pits, then pale khaki on top edges.
pitted-green-armour.green armour with corrosion pits: Run a warm brown wash into the panel lines and pits after stippling the green, then pale khaki on the top edges.

red-gem.red gem: Paint it black, glaze deep red drawn down to the bottom, add orange then peach in the bottom corner, and a white glint.
red-gem.ruby: Black, then thin deep red layers drawn downwards, peach in the bottom corner, and white on the bottom edge and a dot at the top corner.
red-gem.how to paint a gem: Paint it black, glaze colour down to the bottom getting lighter lower, add a pale highlight in the bottom corner, then a white glint.
red-gem.red jewel: Black first, thin deep red glazes lighter towards the bottom, orange and peach low down, and a white dot at the top corner.
red-gem.gem with a white glint: After the red and peach, add a touch of white on the bottom edge and a dot at the top corner.
red-gem.make gems look like glass: Keep the light at the bottom: black, red glazes lighter lower down, peach in the bottom corner, and a white dot at the top.
red-gem.ruby on a sword: Black, then deep red glazes drawn down, orange and peach in the bottom corner, and a white glint at the top corner.
red-gem.red gemstone tutorial: Black base, deep red glazes each lighter red lower, orange and peach in the bottom corner, then white on the bottom edge and top corner.
red-gem.gem looks flat: Paint it black first, then glaze thin red towards the bottom so it gets lighter lower, with peach low and a white glint at the top.
red-gem.how to paint jewels: Black base, thin colour glazes lightening towards the bottom, a pale bottom corner, then a white touch and dot.

tarnished-gold.old tarnished gold: Dark brownish gold base, warm gold highlights, a dark green brown wash dabbed off the high points, then pale greyish gold on top.
tarnished-gold.make gold look ancient: Dark brownish gold base, warm gold highlights, then a dark green brown wash dabbed off high points and pale greyish gold edges.
tarnished-gold.dirty grimy gold: Wash dark green and brown over it and dab it off the high points, then edge only the highest points in a pale greyish gold.
tarnished-gold.gold looks too shiny and new: Darken the base with brown, wash it dark green brown, and finish paler and duller than new gold.
tarnished-gold.greenish antique gold: Wash it dark green brown, dab the high points, and edge pale greyish gold rather than bright gold.
tarnished-gold.dull aged gold for a tomb: Wash dark green brown over a dark brownish gold and wipe it off high points before it dries.
tarnished-gold.how do i weather gold: Dark brownish gold, warm gold highlights, a dark green brown wash wiped back, then pale greyish gold on the highest points.
tarnished-gold.treasure that looks centuries old: Wash it with dark green, brown wash and water, dab it off the high points, then edge pale greyish gold.
tarnished-gold.dark wash on gold wiped back: Dark brownish gold, warm gold highlights, a dark green brown wash dabbed back, and pale greyish gold on the highest points.
tarnished-gold.old gold armour: Mix dark green, brown wash and water, brush it on, and dab it off the high points before it dries.

warm-copper.copper trim: Copper brown base, a warm brown wash, dark burgundy glaze at rivets and low down, then pale gold and gold silver edges.
warm-copper.how to paint copper: Base copper mixed with mid brown, wash warm brown, glaze dark burgundy low down, and edge in warm gold then gold and silver.
warm-copper.warm copper pipes: Copper brown base, warm brown wash, dark burgundy glaze heavier at rivets and on lower parts, then pale gold edges.
warm-copper.stipple copper: For speed, stipple steel and tint it copper with a warm brown wash or one coat paint.
warm-copper.copper looks too pink: See: deep warm copper, built from copper brown with a warm brown shade and burgundy glaze.
warm-copper.old copper armour: Copper brown base, warm brown wash, then a dark burgundy glaze heavier at rivets and on the lower parts.
warm-copper.tint steel to copper: Stipple steel, tint it copper, then shade warm brown and glaze dark burgundy at rivets and low down.
warm-copper.copper recipe: Copper brown, a warm brown shade, a dark burgundy glaze, then edges of warm gold and a gold and silver mix.
warm-copper.copper with a brown wash: Wash warm brown over it all, then brush thin copper back onto the flats to bring back the shine.
warm-copper.steampunk copper: Copper brown base, warm brown wash, dark burgundy at rivets and lower parts, then pale gold edges.

yellow-cloth.yellow cloth: Pale warm yellow over a sandy brown primer, golden yellow wash, orange brown in the deepest folds, then pale yellow highlights.
yellow-cloth.how do i paint yellow robes: Base pale warm yellow over sandy brown, wash golden yellow, shade orange brown in deep folds, and layer pale yellow on raised folds.
yellow-cloth.yellow cloak: Pale warm yellow base, golden yellow wash, orange brown in the deep folds and hems, then pale yellow on the raised folds.
yellow-cloth.yellow tabard: Pale warm yellow base, golden yellow wash, orange brown in the folds and hems, then pale yellow blended on the raised folds.
yellow-cloth.warm yellow fabric: Pale warm yellow over sandy brown primer, a golden yellow wash, orange brown shading and pale yellow highlights.
yellow-cloth.yellow that covers well: Mix sandy yellow with pale yellow over a sandy brown primer; it covers in two coats.
yellow-cloth.rich yellow clothes: Pale warm yellow, golden yellow wash, orange brown in the deepest folds, then lighter steps of pale yellow on raised folds.
yellow-cloth.yellow cloth looks thin: Use a sandy brown primer and mix sandy yellow with pale yellow; it covers in two coats.
yellow-cloth.golden yellow robe: Pale warm yellow, a golden yellow wash for colour and soft shadow, orange brown in the deep folds, then pale yellow highlights.
yellow-cloth.yellow banner: Pale warm yellow base, golden yellow wash, orange brown along the folds and hems, then pale yellow on the raised areas.

airbrush-cleaning.clean airbrush between colours: Tip out leftover paint, add water, back bubble two or three times, use cleaner if needed, then spray clean water through.
airbrush-cleaning.how to back bubble: Cover the nozzle with a finger, cloth or soft sponge and pull the trigger so air pushes back through the cup, then tip it out.
airbrush-cleaning.airbrush keeps clogging: Clean after every colour so paint never dries inside, and check paint thickness, pressure, needle seating and a tight nozzle cap.
airbrush-cleaning.flush an airbrush with water: Add water to the cup, spray or tip it out into a cleaning pot, then back bubble until it comes out clean.
airbrush-cleaning.airbrush colors mixing in the cup: Tip out the leftover paint, wipe the cup, and flush water and cleaner through after each colour, back bubbling until clean.
airbrush-cleaning.dried paint inside airbrush: Add cleaner, scrub the bottom of the cup with an old brush, bubble it, then spray clean water through.
airbrush-cleaning.how often should i clean my airbrush: Between every colour and at the end of each session; a quick rinse is enough between similar colours, but dark to white needs a full clean.
airbrush-cleaning.flakes coming out of the nozzle: Avoid blowing leftovers out through the nozzle, which pushes flakes into the tip; tip them out and wipe the cup instead.
airbrush-cleaning.airbrush cleaning routine: Tip out the paint, rinse with water, back bubble, use cleaner if needed, and test spray water on card before the next colour.
airbrush-cleaning.changing colour in an airbrush: Tip out the old paint, flush water through, back bubble until clean, then spray water on card to check it mists evenly.

airbrush-tinting.airbrush glaze: Thin it far more than usual so it only stains paper, then mist light passes with a fine needle at low pressure, letting each dry.
airbrush-tinting.how thin for airbrush glazing: About one part paint or ink to six to twelve parts thinner and water, plus a drop of matt medium; it should only stain paper.
airbrush-tinting.tinting with an airbrush: Mist very thin colour in light passes, letting each dry, lighter transparent colours first and darker ones after.
airbrush-tinting.airbrush ink: Thin ink about one part to six to twelve parts thinner and water, add a drop of matt medium, and spray in light passes.
airbrush-tinting.smooth colour shift airbrush: Block in tones by brush, then mist thin glazes over the joins in light passes, letting each dry.
airbrush-tinting.spray glow effect: Brush the source white first, then mist colour over it and just around it, repeating for a stronger effect.
airbrush-tinting.airbrush filter: One or two light passes over the whole area pull rough layers together, add saturation and knock highlights back.
airbrush-tinting.airbrush wash: Most ready washes spray as they are; mist from below or at a steep angle into the shadows to add depth.
airbrush-tinting.thinning ratio for airbrush glazes: About one part paint or ink to six to twelve parts thinner and water; one coat contrast style paints need about two to four parts.
airbrush-tinting.spray thin layers of colour: Thin far more than usual, use low pressure, make a light pass, let it dry, and build the colour in two to four passes.

applying-washes.how to apply a wash: Load a medium brush with a good belly, place the wash into recesses or flood it, hold one angle until dry, and lift pools.
applying-washes.washing a model: Flood the wash over busy areas, place it precisely on big flat panels, and lift any pools before they dry.
applying-washes.wash pools everywhere: Press a blotted brush into each pool to lift it, and watch the bottom of folds and parts that hang down.
applying-washes.how much wash should i use: Load the brush full but not dripping, and use two thin washes rather than one heavy one for more control.
applying-washes.wash left rings: Rings come from brushing into wash that has started to dry, or a tiny brush running dry; use a bigger brush and keep wet meeting wet.
applying-washes.shading with a wash: Push the wash towards the spot and lift off where you want it darkest; it gathers where the brush leaves.
applying-washes.best brush for washes: A medium or larger brush with a good belly, ideally an older synthetic one; a tiny brush runs dry and leaves rings.
applying-washes.applying shade properly: Shake the wash, load from a palette, place it where you want shadow, hold the model at one angle and lift pools.
applying-washes.how do i do a wash without tide marks: Use a big enough brush, work in small sections so wet meets wet, never brush into drying wash, and lift pools.
applying-washes.wash technique for beginners: Shake it, load a medium brush, flood busy areas or place it in recesses, hold one angle until dry, and lift pools.
applying-washes.How do I use a wash for shading?: Touch the wash into the recesses, push it towards where you want it darkest and lift off there, then let it dry fully.

basing-finishing-touches.base looks unfinished: Carry the texture right to the edge, paint everything on it, tie it together with a brown wash and pale drybrush, and paint a clean rim.
basing-finishing-touches.sand stuck on the base rim: Wipe sand off the rim while the glue is wet, or scrape it off later before painting the rim.
basing-finishing-touches.what colour should the base rim be: See: the rim needs two thin coats, painted last and stopping at the top edge; this entry does not name a colour.
basing-finishing-touches.make my bases look tidy: Keep sand off the rim and rocks, spread glue flat, paint every bit of the base, and finish with a clean rim in two thin coats.
basing-finishing-touches.ground should run to the edge of the bas: Run the texture, cracks and colour right up to the edge, as if the ground carries on beyond it.
basing-finishing-touches.neaten up base edges: Scrape texture off the side of the rim, then paint the rim last in two thin coats, stopping at the top edge.
basing-finishing-touches.debris piles around rocks: Yes: debris piles around objects rather than on top of them, so heap it at the foot of the rocks.
basing-finishing-touches.how do i finish off a base: Carry the ground to the edge, give it all a brown wash and pale bone drybrush, add tufts in the dips, then paint the rim last.
basing-finishing-touches.base rim painting: Scrape off any texture first, then paint it last in two thin coats, stopping at the top edge; satin suits a smooth rim, matt a rough one.
basing-finishing-touches.messy sand creeping up the rocks: Nudge the sand back down off the rocks, and keep the glue slightly back from details so it does not creep.

black-out-stage.black out stage: Once the main colour is done, paint everything else black so the model reads clearly and the details are easier to finish.
black-out-stage.paint everything else black: Paint the straps, pouches, guns, undersuit and metal parts black after the main colour, working in big chunks.
black-out-stage.model looks messy halfway: Black out everything but the main colour; it stops the one colour blob look and shows clearly what is left to paint.
black-out-stage.black lining the gaps: Run slightly thinned black into the cracks and between areas; it leaves neat dark lines with very little effort.
black-out-stage.tidy a model with black: Paint every part but the main colour black, then run thinned black between garments and around belts.
black-out-stage.how do i make details read clearly: Black out everything but the main colour, then pick out the details; the dark areas separate the parts so they read clearly.
black-out-stage.blacking out straps and guns: Paint straps black in big chunks, and paint guns black all over, then pick out only the raised metal parts.
black-out-stage.black undersuit before detail: Paint the whole undersuit black in big chunks, then add back the few strips of main colour that show.
black-out-stage.thinned black into cracks: Slightly thinned black runs into the cracks and leaves neat dark lines between areas with very little effort.
black-out-stage.why paint parts black after the main col: It stops the model looking like one colour blob, shows what is left to paint and helps you judge contrast.

brighten-dark-schemes.dark uniform looks muddy: Paint the main colour a little brighter than the reference, then add small bright details like cords, cuffs or piping.
brighten-dark-schemes.historical models look too dark: Small models look darker than they are, so paint the main colour a little brighter and lighter than the real reference.
brighten-dark-schemes.brighten dark green uniforms: Paint the green a little brighter and lighter than the reference, in at least two thin coats over black primer, then wash it back down.
brighten-dark-schemes.model is a blob at arm's length: Push the main colour brighter and pick out small bright details such as coloured cords, cuffs or white piping.
brighten-dark-schemes.dark colours merge together: Pick out small bright details such as coloured cords, cuffs or white piping to separate the dark areas.
brighten-dark-schemes.napoleonic uniform too dark: Paint it a little brighter than the real reference, and pick out bright cuffs, cords and white piping to break it up.
brighten-dark-schemes.how to make dark schemes readable: Push the colours brighter than reality and add small bright details so the dark areas separate.
brighten-dark-schemes.black uniform painting: See: brighten dark uniforms and highlight black straps with a few short dark grey lines.
brighten-dark-schemes.scale colour for dark colours: Paint dark colours a little brighter and lighter than the real thing, as small models look darker than they are.
brighten-dark-schemes.dark scheme looks flat: Brighten the main colour and add small bright details such as cuffs, cords or white piping to break up the dark areas.

building-a-gaming-board.build a gaming table: Glue foam tiles onto a flat board, cut in levels, spread filler for toughness, add sand and grit, then prime, drybrush and wash.
building-a-gaming-board.foam board terrain: Glue polystyrene tiles on wood, cut levels, toughen with household filler, and texture it with sand, grit and small stones.
building-a-gaming-board.make my own game board: Glue foam on a wooden board, cut levels, cover the ground in filler, add sand and grit with watered PVA, then prime and paint.
building-a-gaming-board.polystyrene tiles for a table: Glue the foam tiles onto a solid flat board such as an old table top, then cut levels into them.
building-a-gaming-board.sunken road on a board: Mark the road on the foam, cut the foam down into a lower level, and cover it with textured plastic sheet such as cobbles.
building-a-gaming-board.light but tough gaming board: Foam tiles keep it light, and household filler spread over the open ground makes the soft foam much tougher.
building-a-gaming-board.textured board with sand: Brush on watered PVA and scatter mixed grades of sand, grit and small stones so the ground is not one even texture.
building-a-gaming-board.how do i make a war games table: Glue foam tiles on a flat board, cut levels, fix buildings, toughen with filler, add sand and grit, then prime and paint.
building-a-gaming-board.terrain board from insulation foam: Cut 5 cm rigid insulation foam into panels and hinge them with tape on both faces so they fold up.
building-a-gaming-board.diy battle mat alternative: Lay a fleece cloth over foam offcuts or books for rolling hills, or trim fake fur fabric to grass height and airbrush it.

carving-stone-and-cracks.carve stone blocks: Score the joints between blocks with a needle so each stone reads as its own piece, then soften the edges.
carving-stone-and-cracks.how do i carve cracks in a base: Cut a few cracks with a sharp knife tip along lines of stress, then widen and soften them with the side of the blade.
carving-stone-and-cracks.plaster bases: Plaster is cheap: carve single stones, or cast a slab in a frame and cut whole bases from it.
carving-stone-and-cracks.stonework texture: Score irregular blocks into plaster or hard putty, cut a few cracks, and soften the edges for age.
carving-stone-and-cracks.cracked stone basing: Cut a few cracks from a corner or impact point with a knife tip, then widen and soften them with the side of the blade.
carving-stone-and-cracks.score bricks into putty: Cover a core in epoxy putty and score the brick lines with a blade.
carving-stone-and-cracks.carving slate effect: See: carving stone and cracks into plaster or hard putty, in this entry.
carving-stone-and-cracks.ruined wall texture: Score blocks, cut short Y shaped cracks, lift out a small piece and glue it back slightly apart.
carving-stone-and-cracks.stone slab bases from plaster: Cast a plaster slab in a frame, cut bases from it, then score blocks and cut cracks.
carving-stone-and-cracks.make cracks look natural: Use a few cracks along lines of stress, such as out from a corner or impact, rather than random zigzags.

choosing-a-wash-colour.which wash colour: Pick the wash that matches what the base colour becomes in shadow: warm brown for warm colours, a deep version of the colour for cool ones.
choosing-a-wash-colour.what wash to use on red: A warm brown wash, as a mid red darkened drifts towards deep brown; black can make it look dirty and grey.
choosing-a-wash-colour.black or brown wash: Brown for reds, oranges, yellows, wood, skin and most vehicle panels; black or dark blue grey for steel and cool greys.
choosing-a-wash-colour.wash makes it look dirty: One wash over the whole model makes every colour look a little dirty; give each colour group its own wash.
choosing-a-wash-colour.wrong wash colour: Ask what the base colour turns into when it darkens and use a wash that matches it.
choosing-a-wash-colour.wash for blue armour: Use a deep version of the blue itself rather than black.
choosing-a-wash-colour.what shade for skin: A warm brown wash suits skin; thin a skin wash with medium and build it in coats on pale skin.
choosing-a-wash-colour.wash for metal: Black or a dark blue grey for steel, a warm chestnut for gold, and purple or crimson to add depth to gold.
choosing-a-wash-colour.choose the right shade: Match the wash to the colour the base turns into in shadow, and give each colour group its own wash.
choosing-a-wash-colour.wash turned my red grey: Black can make red look dirty and grey; a warm brown wash suits red better.

cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.lining spilled onto the panel: Let it dry, then paint the base or soft shade colour back over the overspill, cutting the line back to where it belongs.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.wash went onto raised areas: Once dry, paint the base colour back over the flats, stopping just short of the recess to leave a thin band of shade.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.fix messy panel lines: Let it dry, then paint the lighter colour back over the overspill, cutting the line back to where it belongs.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.highlight paint got in the recess: Mix the shade colour with a little black and paint it back into the recesses.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.tidy up shading mistakes: Cut spilled lining back with the lighter colour, and paint a dark mix back into recesses that caught highlight paint.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.black lining too thick: Paint the base or soft shade colour back over the edges of the line to cut it back to the width you want.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.clean up after recess shading: Paint the base colour back over the flats, stopping just short of the recess, and do it before highlighting.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.paint back over a sloppy wash: Once dry, paint the base back over the raised areas, leaving a thin band of shade in the recess.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.dark line went over the edge: Paint the lighter base or shade colour back over the overspill once dry, cutting the line back.
cleaning-up-lines-and-recesses.how do i fix messy lining: Let it dry, then paint the lighter colour back over the overspill, cutting the line back to where it belongs.

colour-variation-in-skin.skin looks flat: Tint set zones with very thin glazes: deep red around nose and mouth, cool blue grey near the eyes, and yellow where bone sits close.
colour-variation-in-skin.how do i add colour to skin: Glaze thin reds, blues and purples into set zones of the face and body, mixed partly from the skin tone so no change is abrupt.
colour-variation-in-skin.red cheeks and nose: Glaze deep red mixed with skin tone around the nose, mouth and cheekbone shadows, not on the cheeks themselves; go lightly on the nose.
colour-variation-in-skin.blue stubble on face: Glaze a thin cool grey blue or green on the sides and lower third of the face to suggest stubble.
colour-variation-in-skin.skin zones glazes: Yellow forehead, red band across nose, cheeks and ears, cooler duller chin, and blue or purple in the deep body shadows.
colour-variation-in-skin.realistic skin tones: Real skin shows warm and cool zones, so add them with very thin glazes of reds, blues and purples, then glaze highlights back over.
colour-variation-in-skin.warm and cool skin: Keep yellow where bone sits close, red on elbows, knees and the nose band, and blue or purple in deep shadow.
colour-variation-in-skin.face looks one colour: Glaze set zones of the face in thin reds, blues and purples rather than one brown wash, then glaze the highlights back over.
colour-variation-in-skin.make skin less boring: Add thin warm and cool glazes in zones, such as red around the nose and mouth and a hint of cool blue under the eyes.
colour-variation-in-skin.skin color variation: Glaze warm and cool zones thinly, then glaze the highlight colours back over so the colour looks under the skin, not on top.

common-beginner-mistakes.beginner mistakes: Thick paint, unmixed pots, rushing and overworking cause most early problems; thin your paint, shake the pots, slow down and know when to stop.
common-beginner-mistakes.paint too thick: Thin it on the palette to roughly the flow of milk and build colour in two or more thin coats.
common-beginner-mistakes.my paint looks like jam: Paint that thick clumps and hides detail; thin it to roughly the flow of milk and build up two or more thin coats.
common-beginner-mistakes.why does my model look bad: Usually thick paint, unmixed pots or rushed strokes; thin it, shake every pot, slow down and do one or two areas per session.
common-beginner-mistakes.first model tips: Thin paint to milk, shake every pot, use paint made for models, slow down, and call it done rather than reworking it.
common-beginner-mistakes.paint streaky and clumpy: Thick paint clumps and streaks, so thin it to about the flow of milk and shake or stir every pot first.
common-beginner-mistakes.new to painting what not to do: Avoid thick paint, unshaken pots, open lids, craft paint, rushing and overworking a nearly finished model.
common-beginner-mistakes.detail disappeared under paint: Thick paint hides detail like crayon; thin it to roughly the flow of milk and build two or more thin coats.
common-beginner-mistakes.paint looks lumpy: Thin the paint to about the flow of milk and build two or more thin coats; thick paint clumps and streaks.
common-beginner-mistakes.common mistakes painting minis: Thick paint, unstirred pots, open lids, craft paint, rushed strokes, over thinned paint and reworking a finished model.

crackle-paint-problems.crackle paint not cracking: Use it thick, with no water and little added colour, on a primed surface; thin coats or water stop it cracking well.
crackle-paint-problems.cracks too small: Thin coats give fine cracks; lay it thicker, or add a second coat over the dry first one, for big chunks.
crackle-paint-problems.crackle paste runny: Spread some on card for a few minutes to thicken it, or use the thicker paste gathered in the lid, and never add water.
crackle-paint-problems.how to get big cracks: Lay it thick, or add a second coat over the first or over still wet basing paste, for wider, deeper cracks.
crackle-paint-problems.crackle not working: Use it thick with no water, little added colour or fine soil, over primer rather than varnish, and dab it on.
crackle-paint-problems.crackle went smooth: See: crackle needs a thick layer with no water or fine soil, as thin, runny paste gives tiny cracks.
crackle-paint-problems.thick crackle for bigger cracks: Thicker areas dry slower and split into bigger cracks, so pile it up for a big split.
crackle-paint-problems.hair dryer on crackle: A hair dryer on low, held back and kept moving, speeds it up without harm.
crackle-paint-problems.why didnt my crackle crack: It was likely too thin, watered down, or mixed with too much paint or fine soil; use it thick, straight from the pot.
crackle-paint-problems.crackle paint tiny cracks only: Runny paste and thin coats give tiny cracks, so thicken it on card first and lay it thicker.

damp-drybrushing.drybrush looks chalky: Keep a little moisture in the brush so more than dusty pigment reaches the model, and build up in several light passes.
damp-drybrushing.damp drybrushing: Work a drop of water into a sponge, touch the brush to it before and after loading, and build up several light passes.
damp-drybrushing.smoother drybrush: Keep the brush faintly damp from a moist sponge, build several faint passes letting each dry, and finish paler on smaller areas.
damp-drybrushing.how to drybrush without dust: A slightly damp brush stops only dusty pigment reaching the model; touch it to a moist sponge before and after loading.
damp-drybrushing.dry brush streaks: Work the paint in on smooth laminated card rather than paper towel, keep the brush faintly damp, and use light passes.
damp-drybrushing.softer dry brushing: Keep the brush faintly damp from a sponge, use a larger soft round brush, and build several light passes.
damp-drybrushing.drybrushing gradient: Build several faint passes, letting each dry, then go paler over less of the area until only edges and corners catch.
damp-drybrushing.chalky dry brush fix: Chalkiness comes from a fully dry brush; touch it to a damp sponge before and after loading so it feels faintly cool.
damp-drybrushing.wet dry brush: Faintly damp only: touch it to a sponge with one drop of water, and never dunk it in the water pot.
damp-drybrushing.too dusty drybrush: A completely dry brush leaves only dusty pigment; keep a little moisture in it from a damp sponge.

disguising-rough-sculpts.bad sculpt: Use smooth blends instead of heavy drybrushing, add small speckles over rough skin, and give the face a strong expression.
disguising-rough-sculpts.old lumpy model: Build gradual thin blends rather than drybrushing, add small freehand speckles, and put a clear expression in the eyes.
disguising-rough-sculpts.hide poor detail: Paint part of an awkward shape truly matt black so it reads as shadow, and use blends and speckles to distract the eye.
disguising-rough-sculpts.soft detail on old models: Build those areas with smooth blends, use highlight placement to reshape them, and draw the eye with a strong expression.
disguising-rough-sculpts.make a rough model look good: Use smooth blends, small speckles and a strong expression to draw the eye away, and lean into odd features boldly.
disguising-rough-sculpts.lumpy skin: Use gradual thin blends instead of drybrushing, and add small freehand speckles, freckles or spots to break up the surface.
disguising-rough-sculpts.old metal models look bad: Paint them with smooth blends, a little extra saturation and a clear expression in the eyes to make them look more modern.
disguising-rough-sculpts.how to paint a bad sculpt: Blend smoothly rather than drybrushing, add speckles, hide awkward shapes in matt black, and add saturation and expression.
disguising-rough-sculpts.drybrushing shows every bump: Heavy drybrushing shows up every bump; build those areas with gradual thin blends instead.
disguising-rough-sculpts.low quality sculpt: Blend smoothly, add speckles over rough areas, paint awkward shapes matt black, and lean into odd features.

drybrushing.drybrushing: Wipe almost all the paint off a soft round brush and skim it lightly over raised detail so only edges and texture catch colour.
drybrushing.dry brushing: Load just the tip, wipe until almost nothing comes off, then skim across raised detail so only edges and texture pick up colour.
drybrushing.drybrush looks chalky and grainy: A trace of moisture stops the chalky look; use a soft round brush rather than a small stiff flat for a smoother finish.
drybrushing.how much paint on a drybrush: Load just the tip, then wipe it on card until almost nothing comes off; it should barely mark the back of your hand.
drybrushing.what brush for drybrushing: A soft round drybrush or cheap synthetic makeup brush, kept just for drybrushing, in a few sizes.
drybrushing.quick highlights on fur and texture: Drybrush one step lighter than the base, building two or three passes; it suits fur, chainmail and texture.
drybrushing.drybrush too dusty: Wipe more paint off, keep a trace of moisture in the brush, and use a soft round brush rather than a stiff flat.
drybrushing.makeup brush drybrush: Yes: cheap synthetic makeup brushes give a smoother, less grainy finish than small stiff flats.
drybrushing.drybrush rough texture: Use heavier pressure for a scratchy look that suits rock, and brush in circles on rough areas like bases.
drybrushing.how to dry brush properly: Load the tip, wipe almost all paint off, test on your hand, then skim across raised detail, building two or three passes.
drybrushing.How do I drybrush?: Wipe almost all the paint off a soft brush, skim it across raised detail, and build up two or three lighter passes.

dust-weathering.dusty armour: Run very watery sand, khaki or drab brown paint into the recesses and low areas, heavier near the ground and lighter higher up.
dust-weathering.how do i make models look dusty: Thin a dull khaki or sand with about two parts water and run it into recesses, hems, boots and other low areas.
dust-weathering.weathering with thinned paint: Thin ordinary paint about two parts water to one, and run it into recesses and low parts, starting thinner than you think.
dust-weathering.dust on tank: Brush thinned sandy paint downwards on the panels so it gathers low, or airbrush thinned sand enamel low and drag it down.
dust-weathering.dirty boots and cloak hem: Run thinned khaki or brown into the hems and lower legs, then dab pale bone or pot paint on the boots for mud.
dust-weathering.make it look used: Run watery khaki or brown into recesses and low areas, heaviest near the ground, then a light pale bone drybrush low down.
dust-weathering.desert dust weathering: Use watery sand or khaki in the recesses and low parts, heavier near the ground, with a pale bone drybrush on the lowest parts.
dust-weathering.sandy weathering: Thin sand coloured paint with about two parts water and run it into the recesses and low parts where dust settles.
dust-weathering.watered down paint for dust: About two parts water to one of paint, matched to the base; on knees and elbows about five parts water so it only tints.
dust-weathering.vehicle weathering dust: Brush a thinned sandy paint downwards on the panels so it gathers low, and drybrush pale bone on the lowest parts.

evening-out-sheen.patchy shine: Brush one thin coat of clear matte medium or matte varnish over the whole area so it all ends up with one finish.
evening-out-sheen.some areas shiny some matt: Brush a thin coat of matte medium or matte varnish over the whole area to give it a single finish.
evening-out-sheen.uneven sheen: Brush one thin coat of clear matte medium or matte varnish over the whole area, keeping it thin.
evening-out-sheen.wash dried shiny: Brush a thin coat of matte medium or matte varnish over the whole area to even it out.
evening-out-sheen.glossy patches: Brush a thin coat of matte medium or matte varnish over the area, then add final highlights once dry.
evening-out-sheen.fix mixed finishes: Check the colour has not dried dull, then brush one thin coat of matte medium or matte varnish over the whole area.
evening-out-sheen.model has shiny spots: Brush a thin coat of clear matte medium or matte varnish over the area so the shiny and dull patches match.
evening-out-sheen.even out finish: Brush one thin coat of clear matte medium or matte varnish over the whole area, then add final highlights.
evening-out-sheen.shiny wash marks: Brush one thin matte varnish or medium coat over the whole area, keeping it thin so it does not frost.
evening-out-sheen.matte medium over patches: Yes: one thin coat over the whole area evens it out; keep it thin, as thick matte coats can frost and grey the colour.

feathering.feathering: Place paint where the highlight is strongest, then pull its edge out to a soft fade with a clean, just damp brush.
feathering.two brush blending: Lay paint with one brush and pull its edge out with a second damp brush while it is still wet.
feathering.soft fade on skin: Put a little fairly thick paint on the brightest point, then drag its edge outwards with a damp brush so it fades.
feathering.fade out the edge of a layer: Dab and drag the edge outwards with a just damp brush in quick short strokes while the paint is wet.
feathering.blend with a clean damp brush: Place a little paint on the brightest point, then drag the edge out with a damp brush held at a low angle.
feathering.how do i blend without wet blending: Feather it: place one layer and pull its edge out to a soft fade with a clean damp brush.
feathering.pull paint out to a soft edge: Lay a thin film of clean water beside the paint, then pull the paint into it so it fades to clear.
feathering.layer has a hard line: Feather the edge with a damp brush while it is wet, then tidy it with a few glazes or stippled midtones.
feathering.smooth transition with one colour: Place fairly thick paint at the brightest point, then pull its edge out with a damp brush so it fades smoothly.
feathering.feather a shadow: Place the paint at the deepest point of the shadow, then pull its edge outwards with a damp brush while wet.

fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.i hate my paint job: Most models look bad halfway, so keep going, name exactly what bothers you, and fix one thing at a time.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.model looks ugly halfway: Nearly every model has an ugly phase while layers are half built; it usually comes together with highlights and details.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.should i strip my model: Strip only as a last resort; name exactly what bothers you and fix one thing at a time first.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.unhappy with my mini: Put the problem into words, such as contrast, smoothness or messy edges, and fix that one thing.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.painting looks bad: Keep going to the end, then decide if it is colour, contrast or smoothness and fix one thing at a time.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.fix a bad paint job: Name the fault, then fix it: more contrast, a glaze to smooth a blend, or a tidy pass with the base colour.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.ugly phase painting: Nearly every model goes through an ugly phase while layers are half built; keep going and finish before judging it.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.my model looks terrible: Let it dry, take a break, then name exactly what bothers you and fix one thing at a time.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.how do i rescue a model: Name the fault, then add contrast, glaze rough blends, tidy edges with the base colour, or repaint one clashing part.
fix-a-paint-job-you-hate.disappointed with my painting: Most models look bad halfway; put the brush down if impatient, then fix one named problem at a time.

fix-drybrushing-problems.drybrushing blotchy: Blotches come from too much paint; take paint from the edge of a line with the tip, wipe most off, and build light passes.
fix-drybrushing-problems.drybrush streaks: Streaks come from a damp brush or heavy pressure; use a dry brush and a light touch, then glaze the base colour over.
fix-drybrushing-problems.too much paint drybrushing: Pick up only a little from the edge of the paint with the tip, wipe most off, and build several light passes.
fix-drybrushing-problems.drybrushing looks chalky: Chalky usually means the brush is too dry; wipe off on a smooth surface instead of kitchen roll and leave a trace of moisture.
fix-drybrushing-problems.drybrush mistakes: Too much paint, a damp brush, pressing hard and drybrushing over wet paint cause most blotches and streaks.
fix-drybrushing-problems.fix bad drybrushing: Brush a thin wash or see through glaze of the base colour over the area to hide streaks or dustiness.
fix-drybrushing-problems.drybrushing patches: Use less paint and lighter pressure, then glaze the base colour or a thin wash back over to hide the patches.
fix-drybrushing-problems.dry brushing looks messy: Glaze or wash the base colour back over to hide it, then drybrush the highest points again if needed.
fix-drybrushing-problems.drybrush blobs: Too much paint gives blobs; take only a little from the edge of a line with the tip and wipe most off.
fix-drybrushing-problems.why is my drybrushing streaky: Usually a damp brush, hard pressure or a big jump in colour; keep the brush dry, press lightly and add an in between colour.

fix-shiny-finish.wash dried shiny: Brush matt varnish over the shiny areas only; going from gloss to matt often needs two or more coats.
fix-shiny-finish.model is shiny after painting: A matt varnish over the finished, fully dry model evens out the shine in one go.
fix-shiny-finish.paint dried glossy: Brush matt varnish over the shiny areas, checking under a lamp; it may need two or more coats.
fix-shiny-finish.shiny patches on cloth: Brush matt varnish over the shiny patches only, checking under a lamp, two or more coats if needed.
fix-shiny-finish.how to matte down shine: Brush matt varnish over it, or mix a little base paint or matt medium into washes so they dry flatter.
fix-shiny-finish.wash looks glossy on skin: Brush matt varnish over it; next time mix a little base paint or matt medium into the wash so it dries flatter.
fix-shiny-finish.satin sheen i dont want: Mix a matt paint of a close colour into it, or brush matt varnish over the area once dry.
fix-shiny-finish.remove the shine from a mini: Varnish the finished model with an ultra matt varnish, then add gloss back on anything meant to look wet.
fix-shiny-finish.red paint dries shiny: Some reds dry shiny even after a good shake; brush matt varnish over the area once dry.
fix-shiny-finish.shiny wash rings: Paint thinned base colour back over the raised flats, stopping at the edges, then matt varnish.

fixing-eyes.eyes too big: Paint the skin colour back over the edges to narrow them, then tidy the surrounding skin.
fixing-eyes.wonky eyes: Reline with the dark colour, let it dry, and try again, putting the white on in small strokes from the middle outwards.
fixing-eyes.fix eyes: Reline wonky eyes with the dark colour and try again; expect two or three passes.
fixing-eyes.cross eyed miniature: Let the pupils dry, then trim a white back with the dark colour or add white to move a pupil, checking from normal distance.
fixing-eyes.eye white went everywhere: Reline with the dark colour, let it dry and try again, adding white in small strokes from the middle outwards.
fixing-eyes.eyes look googly: Make the eyes smaller by painting skin back over the edges, and use a simple dot for the iris rather than an outlined circle.
fixing-eyes.messed up eyes: Reline with the dark colour and try again; expect two or three passes, and use a dot or short line for the iris.
fixing-eyes.eyes look crazy: Trim them back with the dark colour or skin, and put both irises to the same side so the figure glances sideways.
fixing-eyes.cant reach the eyes: Fill the socket with deep brown or shade and touch in a tiny dot of off white; in deep shadow that is enough.
fixing-eyes.redo eyes: Reline with the dark colour, let it dry, then repaint the white in small strokes from the middle outwards.

freehand-lightning.freehand lightning: Paint short jagged forking lines, building each lighter colour as a thinner line inside the last, with white dots at the bends.
freehand-lightning.paint lightning bolts: Draw a faint branching line of short straight segments, then step lighter colours as thinner lines inside it up to white.
freehand-lightning.lightning on a cloak: Keep it to a few panels, draw forks of short segments in the darkest glow colour, then thinner lighter lines inside each.
freehand-lightning.lightning on a shield: Use a dark base for contrast, draw forking lines of short segments, then build thinner, lighter lines inside them.
freehand-lightning.how to paint forked lightning: One bold line runs the full length with smaller branches leaving it at the sharp bends; build each colour thinner inside the last.
freehand-lightning.storm effect freehand: Thinned dark glow colour round the source, branching lines of short segments, thinner lighter lines inside, then white dots.
freehand-lightning.lightning freehand tips: Look at photos first, let the brush wobble slightly, and use extra branches to hide a wobbly main line.
freehand-lightning.jagged lightning lines: Draw short straight segments that change direction often, rather than smooth curves.
freehand-lightning.lightning bolt design: See: lightning forks with one bold main line and smaller branches leaving it, often at the sharp bends.
freehand-lightning.lightening freehand: Paint short jagged forking lines, building each lighter colour as a thinner line inside the last.

glazing.glazing: Thin paint until it tints like coloured film, wick most off the brush, and apply thin coats, letting each dry.
glazing.what is a glaze: A glaze is a see through layer of thinned paint that tints what is under it without hiding detail.
glazing.glaze vs wash: A glaze is damp on the brush and must not run into recesses; a bit more water and it becomes a wash.
glazing.how thin should a glaze be: Somewhere between three and fifteen parts liquid to one of paint; test rather than trust a ratio.
glazing.glaze medium: Glaze medium keeps a glaze smooth and slower to dry; mix it with paint instead of, or alongside, water.
glazing.soften a harsh highlight: Glaze over it with thin coats, letting each dry, to soften the step.
glazing.tint a colour without hiding detail: Thin the paint to a see through layer, wick most off the brush, and apply thin coats so detail still shows.
glazing.glazes leave tide marks: Too much liquid pools and dries with tide marks; touch the brush on tissue until it is damp, not dripping.
glazing.glaze went patchy: Patchy glazes usually come from paint too thick or glazing over half dry paint; thin more and let each layer dry.
glazing.smooth the step between two layers: Glaze thinned paint over the join in several thin layers, letting each dry fully.

glowing-light-sources.make a light look like its glowing: Paint the source solid white, pick its brightest point, then glaze colour over it, deepest away from that point.
glowing-light-sources.how do i paint glowing coils: Paint the coils white, glaze colour over them ending each stroke at the bright spot, and line between them with a darker line.
glowing-light-sources.glowing eyes on a model: Paint them white, glaze the glow colour over, leave the centre almost white, and glaze a faint glow onto the skin around.
glowing-light-sources.lantern glow: Paint the source white, glaze colour over it deepest away from the brightest spot, then glaze a faint glow onto nearby surfaces.
glowing-light-sources.glowing screen on a console: Paint it solid white, glaze colour over it deepest away from the brightest point, and line round it with thinned near black.
glowing-light-sources.glowing gem or orb: Paint it white, pick the brightest point, glaze colour over it deepest away from that point, and leave that spot almost white.
glowing-light-sources.light source looks flat, not bright: Be bold with the last near white step, and line round it with thinned near black, as dark next to bright makes a glow stronger.
glowing-light-sources.painting energy weapon glow: White base, transparent glow colour glazed over it ending at the brightest spot, then near white on the hottest point.
glowing-light-sources.white base for glowing parts: Cover the glowing part in white; over black that takes about three coats that are neither thick nor watery.
glowing-light-sources.plasma coils glow: Paint the coils white in thin coats, glaze the glow colour towards the hottest spot, and separate coils with a fine darker line.

gold-over-silver.gold over silver: Base silver, brush a golden yellow or ochre one coat paint over it, then drybrush bright silver over both metals.
gold-over-silver.quick gold: Base all the metal silver, tint the gold parts with a yellow or ochre one coat paint, then one soft silver drybrush over all.
gold-over-silver.contrast over silver: Brush a golden yellow or ochre contrast style paint over silver; the metal shines through and the tint shades the recesses.
gold-over-silver.yellow tint over silver: A golden yellow or ochre one coat paint over silver gives shaded gold, as the metal shines through.
gold-over-silver.fast gold and silver together: Base every metal silver, tint the gold areas yellow or ochre, then one bright silver drybrush highlights both at once.
gold-over-silver.gold without gold paint: Brush a golden yellow or ochre contrast style paint over silver or gunmetal.
gold-over-silver.how do i do gold fast: Base silver, brush yellow or ochre one coat paint over the gold parts, then drybrush silver over everything.
gold-over-silver.shaded gold for speed: Tint silver with a golden yellow or ochre one coat paint, which shades the recesses for you.
gold-over-silver.tinted silver into gold: Brush a golden yellow or ochre one coat paint over silver; add a little brown ink for a deeper gold.
gold-over-silver.gold looks dull and flat: Add a little brown ink to the yellow, glaze thin red brown for warmth, or drybrush silver mixed with yellow on the edges.

hairspray-chipping.hairspray chipping: Paint the chip colour, seal it, add hairspray in two thin coats, paint the top colour, then scrub chips with a damp brush.
hairspray-chipping.chipping fluid: Apply chipping medium in two thin coats over a sealed base, paint the top colour, then wet and scrub after about 20 minutes.
hairspray-chipping.realistic paint chips on a tank: Paint over a resist, scrub it back with a damp brush, and keep chips small on edges, fronts and panel bottoms.
hairspray-chipping.scratch paint back to show metal: Scratch fully dry paint with a hobby knife tip or sandpaper, or use a resist under the top colour and scrub it back.
hairspray-chipping.how do i do the hairspray technique: Base the chip colour, satin varnish it, add two thin hairspray coats, paint the top colour, wet it and scrub with an old brush.
hairspray-chipping.chips look painted on: Use a resist under the top colour and scrub it back so the chips are real, keeping them small and on worn edges.
hairspray-chipping.scrubbing paint off with a damp brush: After about 20 minutes, wet a small area and scrub with a damp old brush or toothpick to lift the top colour.
hairspray-chipping.worn paint showing rust underneath: Base dark brown or dull silver stippled with orange brown, seal it, add a resist, paint the top colour and scrub it back.
hairspray-chipping.hair spray weathering: Spray two thin coats of hairspray over a sealed base, paint the top colour, then wet and scrub it back.
hairspray-chipping.chipped paint on a vehicle: Use a resist under the top colour and scrub chips back on edges, fronts and panel bottoms, keeping them small.

highlighting-tiny-details.highlighting vents: Keep the highlights on vents very fine, using only the tip of the brush, and skip some edges if needed.
highlighting-tiny-details.rivets look too bright: Do not base and wash them; leave them in the surrounding colour and dot each with bright metal at the end.
highlighting-tiny-details.grilles look pale: Each edge packed close adds up to a pale patch, so keep the lines as fine as you can and skip some edges.
highlighting-tiny-details.highlight tiny details: Use only the very tip of the brush, keep lines as fine as possible, and skip some edges if needed.
highlighting-tiny-details.small details too bright: Keep highlights much finer than on large panels, or the many close edges add up to a lighter patch.
highlighting-tiny-details.how do i edge highlight rivets: Leave rivets in the surrounding colour and dot each with bright metal at the end rather than lining them.
highlighting-tiny-details.vents went chalky: Many edges packed close turn the area pale; keep highlights very fine with the brush tip and skip some edges.
highlighting-tiny-details.rows of detail look lighter: Make each highlight much finer than on a large panel, and skip some edges so the area does not turn pale.
highlighting-tiny-details.fine highlights on small bits: Use only the very tip of the brush, with good light and magnification, and keep the lines as fine as you can.
highlighting-tiny-details.grill highlights: Keep grille highlights very fine with just the tip of the brush, skipping some edges, so the area does not go pale.

hovering-models.make a model hover: Fix it to a tall piece of terrain on its base, such as a wall corner, tree stump or small rock, pinned at a hidden contact point.
hovering-models.floating model without flying stand: Pin it to a tall scrap of terrain on the base, joined at a hidden point such as the back of a pack or a trailing foot.
hovering-models.levitating model: Join it to a tall piece of terrain at a hidden contact point and pin the joint with wire for strength.
hovering-models.model floating on a rock: Hold a tall rock against it to check the height, trim the rock inside the base edge, then pin the model to it at a hidden point.
hovering-models.how do i make a flyer without a clear st: Fix it to a tall piece of terrain such as a wall corner, tree stump or rock, joined at a hidden contact point and pinned.
hovering-models.jump pack model hovering: Join a hidden point such as the back of the pack to a tall piece of terrain on the base, and pin it with wire.
hovering-models.model on a tree stump looks airborne: Cut the stump off its frame, saw it to shape, trim it inside the base edge, and pin a trailing foot or pack to it.
hovering-models.airborne pose on base: Push a tall terrain piece to one side of the base and pin the model to it at a hidden contact point.
hovering-models.hovering wizard: For a figure with no legs, drill a long brass rod into the body as the support and cover the lower body with putty and cloth.
hovering-models.flying model on terrain piece: Fix it to a tall piece of terrain on its base at a hidden contact point and pin the joint with wire.

jagged-edge-highlights.battle damaged edges: Tap the edge highlight on in short broken strokes with the side of the brush, so the gaps read as wear.
jagged-edge-highlights.chipped edge highlights: Tap the highlight on in short broken strokes, and add small dark brown chips beside some of the light marks.
jagged-edge-highlights.broken edge highlight: Lay the side of the brush on the edge and make small taps and flicks along it instead of one clean line.
jagged-edge-highlights.make armour look battered: Tap broken highlights along the edges, mostly upward facing ones, and add small dark brown chips beside some.
jagged-edge-highlights.jagged highlights: Tap the edge highlight on in short broken strokes instead of a neat line, so it looks chipped and battered.
jagged-edge-highlights.edge highlight looks too neat: Instead of one clean line, tap and flick along the edge with the side of the brush.
jagged-edge-highlights.tap the brush along edges: Lay the side of the brush on the edge and make small taps and flicks, with paint at normal layer consistency.
jagged-edge-highlights.worn armour edges: Tap broken highlights on, mostly on upward facing edges and corners, where light and wear would hit first.
jagged-edge-highlights.rough edge highlights: Tap them on with the side of the brush in short broken strokes; gaps and uneven bits read as wear.
jagged-edge-highlights.beaten up armour plates: Tap broken edge highlights on, add small dark brown chips beside some, and a brighter off white on a few clean edges.

layer-and-glaze-blending.blending: Paint solid bands of each colour first, then glaze over each join until it is smooth.
layer-and-glaze-blending.smooth blend: Paint solid bands with small steps between them, then glaze a thinned mix of the two over each join until smooth.
layer-and-glaze-blending.how do i blend colours: Lay solid bands of each colour, then glaze a thinned half and half mix over each join, narrowing the strip each pass.
layer-and-glaze-blending.layering and glazing: Paint solid bands of each colour first, then soften the joins with see through glazes, letting each pass dry.
layer-and-glaze-blending.blending bands of colour: Paint the bands in order, then glaze a thinned mix over each join, feathering the stroke and letting each pass dry.
layer-and-glaze-blending.visible lines between layers: Glaze a thinned mix of the two colours over the line between them, repeating five to eight times.
layer-and-glaze-blending.soften layer joins: Glaze the next colour, or a half and half mix, thinned until see through, over the join, and repeat as it narrows.
layer-and-glaze-blending.glaze blending: Glaze a thinned half and half mix over each join, run a damp brush along its edge, and repeat until smooth.
layer-and-glaze-blending.how to blend on a cloak: Paint solid stripes from dark to light, then glaze thinned mixes over each join, letting each pass dry.
layer-and-glaze-blending.blending stripes: Keep the step between stripes small, then glaze a thinned mix of each pair over their join until it is smooth.

limited-palette.limited palette: Put out around five or six paints plus black and white, mix everything from them, and do not add more.
limited-palette.paint with only five colours: Pick five, such as one warm, one cool, two neutrals and one accent, plus black and white, and mix everything else.
limited-palette.mix everything from a few paints: Use your darkest paint as every shadow and your lightest as every highlight, mixing the rest in between.
limited-palette.restricted palette: Pick around five or six paints plus black and white before you start and mix everything from them.
limited-palette.small paint collection: Keep to a handful of paints, plus black and white; just about five can cover a whole model.
limited-palette.how to get harmony with few paints: Mix everything from a handful of paints so skin, cloth and props share the same mixes and sit together.
limited-palette.too many paints: Put out five or six plus black and white before you start, and mix everything else from them.
limited-palette.limited palette painting: Choose about five or six paints plus black and white, with a clear light to dark run and one accent.
limited-palette.mixing from primaries: See: a classic four colour set of a strong red, black, ivory and yellow ochre, mixed into flesh and off whites.
limited-palette.what paints for a limited palette: One warm, one cool, two neutrals and one accent, or a strong red, black, ivory and yellow ochre.

making-your-own-transfers.make my own decals: Print designs on waterslide decal paper, seal inkjet ink with decal film, and use white sheet for dark surfaces.
making-your-own-transfers.waterslide paper: It comes for inkjet or laser printers, clear or white backed; clear suits light surfaces, white backed suits dark ones.
making-your-own-transfers.print decals at home: Print on waterslide decal paper, repeat the design across the sheet, and seal inkjet ink with decal film before use.
making-your-own-transfers.custom transfers: Design on transparent backgrounds, print on waterslide paper, seal it, and apply over gloss with setting solution.
making-your-own-transfers.decals on dark armour: Use white backed decal sheet on dark surfaces, and put the design on a simple shape like a circle to hide edges.
