painting-fire.flames: Over white, keep pale yellow in the recesses and base, then orange and red towards the tips, darkest at the ends.
painting-fire.how do i paint fire: Undercoat white, base pale yellow, wash warm yellow and orange, stipple orange red from the tips, then soft black ends.
painting-fire.burning effect: Flip normal highlighting: lighter colours low and in recesses, darker ones on ridges and tips, then glaze glow nearby.
painting-fire.flame sword: White core at the base, yellow then orange through the middle, red and soft black at the tips, plus glow on the blade.
painting-fire.fire looks flat: Add thin dark lines on raised ridges and thin pale lines in the folds, then white deep at the base and tiny sparks.
painting-fire.orange fire: Wash warm yellow and orange over a white undercoat, pulling orange towards the tips, then stipple orange red there.
painting-fire.flame coming out of a gun: White at the base, yellow then orange, red and soft black at the tips, then glaze orange onto the nearby metal.
painting-fire.campfire: Pale core low down, orange and red rising, soft black on the tips, a little brownish grey smoke and tiny sparks.
painting-fire.torch flame: White and pale yellow at the core, orange through the middle, red and soft black at the tips, with sparks above.

painting-hands-and-limbs.painting hands: Light the knuckles, fingertips and the back of the hand, and run a fine dark brown line between the fingers.
painting-hands-and-limbs.hands look like blobs: Run a fine line of dark brown between the fingers so they read as separate, and highlight the knuckles and tips.
painting-hands-and-limbs.how to paint fingers: Light the fingertips and knuckles, darken between fingers, and keep pale lines short so fingers stay round.
painting-hands-and-limbs.knuckles highlights: Put the highlights on the knuckles, then a short thin pale line on the upper edge of each.
painting-hands-and-limbs.bare arms: Light the upper part of each muscle and the top of the elbow, leaving the lower part and back in shade.
painting-hands-and-limbs.skin on bare legs: Light the upper part of each muscle and the top of the knee, and leave the back of the leg in shade.
painting-hands-and-limbs.muscle highlights: Light the top of each muscle, as light comes from above, and leave the underside and back of the limb darker.
painting-hands-and-limbs.tiny hands: Ring the light round small limbs with curved strokes, brightest at the top, and darken between the fingers.
painting-hands-and-limbs.where to highlight an arm: On the upper part of each muscle and the top of the elbow. Use ring shaped strokes on small arms.
painting-hands-and-limbs.shading between fingers: Paint a fine line of dark brown between the fingers so they read as separate rather than a mitten.

painting-muscles.muscles: Shade only where forms face down and run the first highlights across neighbouring muscles so the body reads as one shape.
painting-muscles.abs: Do not ring each ab in dark. Keep the gaps that face up at midtone and join the highlights across neighbouring muscles.
painting-muscles.muscle shading: Shade only surfaces facing down, keep upward gaps at midtone, and avoid outlining every muscle in dark.
painting-muscles.muscle highlights: Join neighbouring muscles with early highlights, then save the last one or two brightest steps for single muscles.
painting-muscles.six pack: Do not outline every ab in dark. Keep upward gaps at midtone and join the highlights across the forms.
painting-muscles.chest muscles: Deep shadow goes only under the chest, where forms face down. Highlights join across the chest towards the top.
painting-muscles.muscles look like armour plates: You ringed every muscle with dark. Keep upward gaps at midtone, or shrink shadows to a thin line.
painting-muscles.anatomy painting: Pick a light direction and shade only surfaces that face down, treating skin like a sheet draped over the muscles.
painting-muscles.arm muscles: Light the top of each arm muscle and shade underneath, joining the first highlights across neighbouring forms.
painting-muscles.bare chested barbarian: Shade only where forms face down, join highlights across the muscles, and keep shadows darker low and lighter high.

painting-rust.rust: Build rust in shrinking glazes or dabs from dark brown to bright orange, on edges, rivets and where water sits.
painting-rust.how do i paint rust: Glaze dark brown where water sits and runs, then shrink each layer through mid brown to a bright orange.
painting-rust.rusty metal: Glaze rust from dark brown to bright orange on rivets and seams, then tap bright silver on rubbed edges.
painting-rust.rust streaks running down: Glaze thin dark brown down from fittings, pulling it the way water runs, then fine orange streaks over it.
painting-rust.rust on a tank hull: Put rust where water sits, building dark brown to orange, and haze the paint round it so it does not look stuck on.
painting-rust.realistic rust build up: Start small, build from dark brown to orange in shrinking layers, use two or three tones, and keep it matt.
painting-rust.rusty rivets and seams: Blob thinned orange brown round a rivet and wipe the top clean, then glaze rust out from seams.
painting-rust.make metal look old and rusted: Build rust in shrinking layers from dark brown to orange in pits, seams and under overhangs, and keep it matt.
painting-rust.rust looks like orange blobs: Use two or three tones, stipple patches with deep brown showing, and haze the paint round heavy patches.
painting-rust.too much rust how much to add: Start small, keeping it mostly in shadowed areas and leaving some patches clean. Adding more is easy.

painting-smoke.painting smoke: Base in a tinted dark grey, highlight the top of each puff, keep recesses dark, and go paler towards the far end.
painting-smoke.how do i paint smoke effects: Use tinted greys rather than plain ones, light the top of every puff, and paint glowing smoke white then fluorescent.
painting-smoke.smoke clouds look like grey blobs: Shape every puff: highlight its top with a cool blue grey or warm reddish grey and leave the recesses dark.
painting-smoke.glowing smoke from inside: Darken it, paint near white into the creases under each puff, then cover the white thinly with fluorescent colour.
painting-smoke.magic smoke colours: Wash grey, run a dull and a bright green into the deepest parts, and pick the raised parts out in white.
painting-smoke.smoke plume on a base: Tinted dark grey base, the top of each billow lit, brightest towards the far end where the smoke thins.
painting-smoke.purple tinted grey smoke: Base near black or dark grey with a purple tint, then light the top of each puff with a cool blue grey.
painting-smoke.chimney or exhaust smoke: Purple tinted dark grey, the tops of puffs lit, paler away from the source, and a small glow gap where it rises.
painting-smoke.smoke with fire glowing inside: Near white in the creases under each puff, thin fluorescent over it, darkest across the middle, grey light on top.
painting-smoke.what colours for smoke: A near black or purple tinted dark grey base, with cool blue grey or warm reddish grey on the tops.

painting-terms-glossary.what does wip mean: WIP stands for work in progress: a model or project that is not finished yet.
painting-terms-glossary.what is nmm: NMM, non metallic metal, fakes shiny metal with flat colours and hand painted reflections.
painting-terms-glossary.what is a wash: A wash is thin, see through paint flooded over an area so it runs into the recesses.
painting-terms-glossary.what does glazing mean: Glazing means very thin, see through paint that tints or smooths what is under it.
painting-terms-glossary.painting terminology: See: the glossary in this entry, covering base coat, wash, glaze, value, NMM, OSL, zenithal and more.
painting-terms-glossary.what is a base coat: A base coat is the first solid, even coat of a colour.
painting-terms-glossary.what is value in painting: Value is how light or dark a colour is, ignoring its hue.
painting-terms-glossary.hobby jargon explained: See: plain meanings in this entry for terms like wash, glaze, drybrush, NMM, OSL, zenithal and WIP.
painting-terms-glossary.what does edge highlight mean: A thin bright line painted along sharp edges.
painting-terms-glossary.difference between layering and glazing: Layering builds colour in steps with thinned coats. Glazing uses very thin see through paint to tint or smooth below.

pale-skin.pale skin: Build it from pinks and very pale flesh tones, with cool highlights and warm shadows, and avoid browns.
pale-skin.how do i paint pale skin: Use pinks and very pale tones, add pink with each layer, push cool blue into highlights and keep shadows warm.
pale-skin.fair skin: Build from pinks and very pale flesh, with a touch of cool blue in the highlights and warm shadows.
pale-skin.skin comes out too tanned: Browns add a tan. Use pinks and very pale tones instead, or cool a ready made flesh with light blue.
pale-skin.pale flesh with pink tones: Add a little more pink each layer, and glaze thin magenta into cheeks and lips and grey blue into shadows.
pale-skin.vampire skin: Pale tones, a cold off white on top, and thin magenta and violet glazed into the shadows for a pallid look.
pale-skin.cool skin highlights: Push a little cool blue into the highlights while keeping the shadows warm.
pale-skin.very light skin tone: Lay out about five paints from dark to light, mix half steps between them, and add pink as you go.
pale-skin.pale skin looks orange: Brown and warm tones tan it. Use pinks and very pale tones, and cool flesh with a light blue.
pale-skin.skin for a sickly noble: Pale pinks and flesh tones with thin magenta and violet glazed into the shadows for a pallid look.

picking-models-to-paint.which model should i paint: One you like, with crisp moderate detail, few materials and an open pose your brush can reach.
picking-models-to-paint.good model to practice on: Low cost plastic sets with lively poses let you try techniques without risking an expensive kit.
picking-models-to-paint.what makes a model easy to paint: Crisp detail, a moderate amount of it, mostly one material, and an open pose with nothing blocking the chest.
picking-models-to-paint.best mini for a beginner: A model you like with crisp, moderate detail, few materials and an open pose.
picking-models-to-paint.model too detailed to paint: Detail all over is slow and tiring. Pick moderate detail, or leave parts off while painting to reach them.
picking-models-to-paint.pose too hard to reach with a brush: Leave the blocking part off while painting, or plan to keep the hidden area dark.
picking-models-to-paint.choosing a model with crisp detail: Look for crisp, sharp sculpting with clear edges, which takes washes, drybrushing and one coat paints well.
picking-models-to-paint.fun model to paint: Pick one you like. You will spend hours on it, and liking the design keeps you going.
picking-models-to-paint.simple model to start with: Choose mostly one material, moderate crisp detail, and an open pose your brush can reach.
picking-models-to-paint.should i paint a model i like: Yes, above all. Liking the design keeps you going through the hours of painting.

polymer-clay-sculpting.polymer clay: Smooth unbaked polymer clay with a little odourless solvent, cutting key wrinkles deeper first so they survive.
polymer-clay-sculpting.sculpting with clay: Press volumes on firmly, blend with a rake tool, then soften the surface with a brush and a little odourless solvent.
polymer-clay-sculpting.smooth clay: Stroke it with a soft brush dipped in odourless white spirit and blotted, following the folds. Let it evaporate.
polymer-clay-sculpting.baking clay sculpt: Let the smoothing solvent dry off before baking, and work with the window open.
polymer-clay-sculpting.clay over putty armature: Glue very thin clay sheets with super glue on a slightly smaller patch, and roll them down with a smooth rod.
polymer-clay-sculpting.clay fingerprints: Brush on a little odourless white spirit, blotted on tissue, to soften the top layer so marks melt away.
polymer-clay-sculpting.sculpt cloth wrinkles in clay: Cut wrinkles deeper than you want before smoothing, then re cut any that faded.
polymer-clay-sculpting.how to smooth polymer clay: Blend with a rake tool, then stroke on a little odourless white spirit with a soft brush along the folds.
polymer-clay-sculpting.oven bake clay for miniatures: Press volumes on firmly, smooth with a little solvent, and let it dry off before baking.
polymer-clay-sculpting.clay sculpting tips: Press on firmly, cut wrinkles deeper first, smooth with a little odourless solvent, and add fine wrinkles last.

preparing-resin-models.resin model prep: Check every part, scrub off mould release, cut casting blocks away in small bites, and glue with super glue.
preparing-resin-models.how do i prepare a resin kit: Check the parts, wash them in warm soapy water, cut blocks off in small bites, fill bubbles and dry fit before gluing.
preparing-resin-models.mould release on resin: Mould release blocks primer. Scrub the parts in warm soapy water with an old toothbrush, rinse and dry.
preparing-resin-models.washing resin parts: Scrub them in warm soapy water with an old toothbrush, keeping the casting blocks on as handles, then rinse well.
preparing-resin-models.cutting off casting blocks: Cut in small bites, a little away from the part, with the flat of the cutters towards it, then trim with a knife.
preparing-resin-models.resin part warped: See: noting warped pieces early. This entry says makers usually replace badly cast parts.
preparing-resin-models.what glue for resin: Super glue only. Plastic glue will not bond resin.
preparing-resin-models.primer won't stick to resin: Mould release is the usual cause. Scrub the parts in warm soapy water. If still tacky, ask for a replacement.
preparing-resin-models.missing parts in resin kit: Check every part under good light first. Makers usually replace missing or badly cast parts.
preparing-resin-models.oily feel on new model: A waxy or oily feel means mould release. Scrub it off in warm soapy water with an old toothbrush.

quick-minor-materials.quick small details: Base coat, a thinned darker wash and one bright highlight, or one coat of a one coat paint and one edge highlight.
quick-minor-materials.small leather bits fast: Light tan one coat paint, then dark brown one coat over it once dry. Or warm brown with short hatched highlights.
quick-minor-materials.fast straps and pouches: Paint the whole buckle and strap end metal, drop the strap colour into the middle, then a wash and one highlight.
quick-minor-materials.quick gold trim: A strong single coat gold shaded with a warm brown wash. Mix in a little dark metal if it looks too bright.
quick-minor-materials.speed painting minor details: Base, wash a thinned darker colour, then one bright highlight. Small details matter less than the main areas.
quick-minor-materials.belts and pouches quickly: Paint buckles and strap ends metal, drop the strap colour in, then a wash and one highlight, or a one coat paint.
quick-minor-materials.how to do small metal bits fast: Over black primer, drybrush light grey and add a dark wash, or hatch steel and bright silver on a dark metal.
quick-minor-materials.quick cloth details: Base a grey and add one highlight colour in about three thin passes, each smaller than the last.
quick-minor-materials.details taking too long: Small details matter less. Use base, wash and one highlight, or a one coat paint and an edge highlight.
quick-minor-materials.simple way to paint little bits: A clean base coat, a thinned darker wash and one bright highlight, or a one coat paint with one edge highlight.

reflected-light.reflected light: Add a weak, muted highlight on undersides as if light bounces up from the ground, as a last step.
reflected-light.bounce light: Glaze a thin, muted tone along the undersides of each part, strongest nearest the ground, after normal highlights.
reflected-light.underside highlight: Run a thin glaze of the base colour or a slightly lighter muted tone along the undersides, following the curve.
reflected-light.light from below: Add a weak muted glaze on the undersides, strongest nearest the ground, or a warm glow below for fire.
reflected-light.reflections from the ground: Mix a muted version of the ground colour into the shadow side, strongest on parts nearest the base.
reflected-light.rim light: See: bounce light, a weak muted highlight on undersides, added as the last step after normal highlights.
reflected-light.shiny armour reflection: Shiny surfaces pick up light from below too. Add a weak second highlight on the undersides.
reflected-light.colour bouncing off the base: Mix a muted version of the nearby colour, such as olive green over moss, into the shadow side.
reflected-light.secondary highlight: A weaker highlight on parts facing down, below a dark band under the main top highlight.
reflected-light.advanced lighting: See: bounce light, a weak highlight glazed onto undersides last so shapes look solid and shiny.

resin-printing-setup.resin printer settings: Find the shortest exposure that prints reliably. Test whenever you change resin, and note the settings that work.
resin-printing-setup.exposure time: Aim for the shortest time that prints reliably. Too much or too little exposure both soften detail.
resin-printing-setup.how do i scale prints to match: Measure where a part that fits meets the model, work out the difference as a percentage and scale by that.
resin-printing-setup.3d printing settings for minis: Find the shortest reliable exposure for your resin, test again whenever you change it, and check scale in the slicer.
resin-printing-setup.prints failing: Check room temperature, the resin and a clean, tight vat film before blaming exposure.
resin-printing-setup.exposure test print: Print the zone test card if your printer can, or print one model three times, changing exposure by one second.
resin-printing-setup.printed head too big for body: Measure where a part that fits meets the model, work out the size difference as a percentage, and rescale it.
resin-printing-setup.resin print detail soft: Too much or too little exposure both soften detail. Find the shortest time that still prints reliably.
resin-printing-setup.printer calibration: Run an exposure test, or print one model three times changing exposure a second each time, and retest for new resin.
resin-printing-setup.3d printed miniatures blurry: Exposure too long or short both soften detail. Find the shortest reliable time, and check temperature and vat film.

scratch-building-vehicles.scratch build a vehicle: Build a card core from a template, clad it in plastic sheet, carve tracks from plastic card and add kit parts.
scratch-building-vehicles.build a tank from scratch: Cut a thick card box from a template, clad it in plastic sheet, make tracks from scored plastic card and add spares.
scratch-building-vehicles.card and plasticard tank: Thick card core for the box, plastic sheet over it for armour, scored plastic card tracks and spare kit parts.
scratch-building-vehicles.homemade vehicle: Work from a template, build a card box clad in plastic sheet, and add tracks, rod, tube and spare kit parts.
scratch-building-vehicles.how to make tank tracks: Score 1 mm plastic card between plates with a razor saw, shape the scores with a triangular file, then bend it on.
scratch-building-vehicles.custom vehicle from a template: Use a drawing or printed papercraft template so sides match and corners stay square, rescaling against a real kit.
scratch-building-vehicles.cheap tank build: Plastic sheet is cheap and a mostly card build is nearly free. Card tracks are cheaper but need sealing.
scratch-building-vehicles.how long does a scratch build take: Expect three or four times as long as the kit, about the effort of a heavy conversion.
scratch-building-vehicles.plastic sheet over card core: Build the box from thick card for shape, then clad it in plastic sheet, which takes glue and paint like kit plastic.
scratch-building-vehicles.kitbash bits on scratch build: Spare kit parts close most of the gap: borrow weapons, lights and kit tracks, and add stowage last.

selective-base-coat.selective base coat: Base coat each area but stop short of the deepest recesses so the dark undercoat stays there as shadow.
selective-base-coat.leave black primer in the recesses: Prime dark and base coat each area, letting the brush miss the deep recesses so they read as shadow.
selective-base-coat.black lining shortcut: Leave the dark undercoat in the recesses instead of lining them. It gives clean definition in fewer steps.
selective-base-coat.skip the wash: Base coat over a dark primer, leaving it in the recesses. It replaces the wash and keeps colours bright.
selective-base-coat.base coat but not into the cracks: Paint the raised details and larger upward faces and let the brush miss the deep parts.
selective-base-coat.neat definition without a wash: Base coat each area over a dark primer, stopping short of the recesses so the undercoat gives definition.
selective-base-coat.fast clean look over black: Prime black, base coat each area short of the recesses, and only go back over areas for a brighter highlight.
selective-base-coat.dark undercoat as the shadow: Prime a dark colour and base coat each area, stopping short of the deepest recesses so it stays as shadow.
selective-base-coat.washes make my model grubby: Skip the wash: leave the dark undercoat in the recesses instead. Colours stay bright and clean.
selective-base-coat.let the primer show through: Prime dark and base coat each area short of the deepest recesses. Unpainted parts read as shadow.

simplifying-for-squads.simplify for squads: Cut stages from a display method: drop the middle layers, keep one shade and the edge highlights.
simplifying-for-squads.batch painting: Get the base colour on fast, keep one shade and the edge highlights, and alternate slow steps with quick ones.
simplifying-for-squads.how do i paint squads faster: Drop middle layers, keep one shade and clean edge highlights on the top half, and base coat with a spray.
simplifying-for-squads.too slow for the whole squad: Spray the base colour, keep one wash and the edge highlights, and drop the middle layers.
simplifying-for-squads.display method for troops: Save the full method for leaders and centrepieces. For troops, keep the shade and the edge highlights.
simplifying-for-squads.which steps can i skip: The middle layers between shade and highlight, the first subtle glaze, and highlights on back rank models.
simplifying-for-squads.painting rank and file: Fast base coat, one shade, then one or two clean edge lines only on upward edges of the top half.
simplifying-for-squads.tabletop version of a display recipe: Keep one shade and the edge highlights, drop the middle layers, and use the same colours as your detailed models.
simplifying-for-squads.leaders vs troops detail: Save every stage for leaders. Troops get a fast base, one shade and edge highlights in the same colours.
simplifying-for-squads.fewer steps per model: Merge steps, such as dark grey, a half mix of the middle tones, then light grey, and drop middle layers.

smooth-layering.layer lines: Use more, smaller steps, each covering a little less than the last, and glaze a halfway colour along any visible join.
smooth-layering.smoother layers: Mix more in between tones so each jump is small, make each layer cover a little less, and pull strokes towards the light.
smooth-layering.visible steps in my highlights: Paint a colour halfway between the two layers only along the join, a few times, then a thin glaze of the top tone.
smooth-layering.highlights look stripy: Each pass is covering the same area. Make each layer cover a little less than the last, like roof tiles.
smooth-layering.blocky highlights: The jumps are too big. Mix more in between tones, such as 3 to 1, 2 to 1, 1 to 1 and 1 to 2.
smooth-layering.more steps between layers: Mix base and light at about 3 to 1, 2 to 1, 1 to 1 and 1 to 2, testing each with a dot beside the last layer.
smooth-layering.smoother transitions: Smaller value jumps, each layer covering less, strokes pulled towards the light, and halfway colours along the joins.
smooth-layering.intermediate mixes: Base and light mixed at about 3 to 1, 2 to 1, 1 to 1 and 1 to 2 give an even set of steps.
smooth-layering.hide the lines between layers: Paint a colour halfway between two layers along the join, repeat, then glaze a very thin top tone over it.
smooth-layering.how to make layering smoother: Use more, smaller steps, cover a little less each time, pull strokes towards the light and thin pale steps a bit more.

sponge-chipping.sponge chipping: Dab chips with a torn bit of sponge with most of the paint removed, pressing lightly on edges, then refine some by brush.
sponge-chipping.chipping with foam: Tear firm foam with medium holes, load it, dab most off, then press lightly on edges in a few light passes.
sponge-chipping.quick battle damage: Dab a nearly dry torn sponge on edges and corners where wear happens first, then join some into bigger chips by brush.
sponge-chipping.chip effect on a tank: Sponge very dark brown on edges, lower and front parts, and biggest damage at panel bottoms, rivets and overlaps.
sponge-chipping.sponge weathering: Press a torn sponge, with most paint dabbed off, lightly on edges and corners, building up in light passes.
sponge-chipping.chipped paint fast: Dab most paint off a torn sponge, press it lightly onto edges, then refine a few chips by brush.
sponge-chipping.packing foam chipping: Tear a small piece of packing foam from the middle so it is ragged, then dab most paint off before chipping.
sponge-chipping.chips look like blobs: Too much paint on the sponge. Dab most off on a towel and test on the back of the model first.
sponge-chipping.how to chip with a sponge: Load a torn sponge, dab most off, press straight down lightly on edges and corners, and never drag it.
sponge-chipping.paint chips everywhere: Keep chips small and random, mostly on edges and lower parts. Tidy back an overdone area with the colour underneath.

stacked-edge-highlights.stacked edge highlights: Make the first edge highlight wide, then paint each finer, brighter stage inside it so a sliver of each shows.
stacked-edge-highlights.two stage edge highlight: First a wider half and half mix of base and highlight, then a finer, brighter line inside it on top edges.
stacked-edge-highlights.how do i layer edge highlights: Start with a wide half and half edge, then paint each finer, brighter stage inside the last.
stacked-edge-highlights.edge highlight stages: Wide first stage of base mixed half with highlight, then each later stage finer, brighter and inside the one before.
stacked-edge-highlights.double edge highlight: A wide first edge line, then a finer, brighter one inside it, so a sliver of the first still shows.
stacked-edge-highlights.edge highlight too harsh: Mix the first stage half base, half highlight, and desaturate the final mix slightly so it does not look acidic.
stacked-edge-highlights.thicker then thinner edges: Make the first stage about twice the width of the final line, then each later stage finer and inside the last.
stacked-edge-highlights.edge highlights in stages: Wide first stage, then finer brighter stages inside it, the brightest kept to top edges facing the light.
stacked-edge-highlights.second brighter edge line: Paint it inside the first, finer and less thinned, mostly on top edges facing the light.
stacked-edge-highlights.edge lines brighter: Stack finer, brighter stages inside a wider first line, and finish with pale dots where two edges meet.

straightening-bent-parts.bent spear: Warm the spear in hot water or with a hair dryer until it flexes, ease it straight and hold it as it cools.
straightening-bent-parts.warped resin: Wash it, dip it in hot water for 30 to 60 seconds until it flexes, ease it straight and hold it flat to cool.
straightening-bent-parts.straighten a sword: Warm it in hot water or with a hair dryer, ease it straight against a flat surface, and dip it in cold water to set.
straightening-bent-parts.hot water to bend parts: Dip the part in water from about 70 C up to just boiled for 30 to 60 seconds, ease it straight, then cool it.
straightening-bent-parts.bent part fix: Warm the part gently until it flexes, bend it straight and hold it there as it cools.
straightening-bent-parts.fix warped staff: Dip it in hot water until it flexes slightly, ease it straight against a flat surface, and cool it in cold water.
straightening-bent-parts.resin warp: Warm it in hot water for 30 to 60 seconds, ease it straight and hold it until it cools. Do not overheat resin.
straightening-bent-parts.bent metal blade: Warm soft metal with a hair dryer and ease it back in small steps, without bending one spot back and forth.
straightening-bent-parts.straighten a bent banner pole: Warm it in hot water or with a hair dryer until it flexes, then hold it straight against a flat surface as it cools.
straightening-bent-parts.warped blade arrived bent: Dip it in hot water until it flexes, ease it straight, hold it as it cools, and dip in cold water to set it.

supporting-3d-prints.resin supports: Tilt the model back about 10 degrees, support every island layer by layer, and run supports from the build plate.
supporting-3d-prints.print failed: A missed island prints as a failure or blob. Step through the layers and add a support at every new island.
supporting-3d-prints.islands in a print: Islands start printing before they join the model. Step through the slicer layers and support each new one.
supporting-3d-prints.where to put supports: At every island, plus heavy parts or easy to clean places such as under a base, run from the plate.
supporting-3d-prints.tilt model for printing: Tilt it back about 10 degrees. A steep 45 degree tilt with auto supports often pits the detail on its back.
supporting-3d-prints.blob on resin print: A blob usually means a missed island. Step through the layers and support each new island.
supporting-3d-prints.auto supports not working: Auto supports on a steep tilt often pit the back. Tilt about 10 degrees and add supports at missed islands.
supporting-3d-prints.what angle to print a mini: Tilt it back about 10 degrees rather than a steep 45, which often pits detail on its back.
supporting-3d-prints.supports from the build plate: Run supports from the build plate, not from one part of the model to another, so cleanup is easier.
supporting-3d-prints.my resin print has holes: See: island support, as a missed island in this entry prints as a failure or blob. Support every new island.

texture-in-scale.model looks like a toy: Chunky scratches and texture make a model look like a toy. Keep marks fine, getting finer each stage.
texture-in-scale.scratches too big: Keep scratches fine. Only the first stage can be slightly chunky, and each later one goes finer inside it.
texture-in-scale.texture too chunky: Keep it fine enough to suit the model's size, with each lighter stage finer and closer to the edge.
texture-in-scale.how fine should texture be: Fine enough to suit the model's size. The first stage can be slightly chunky, each later one finer.
texture-in-scale.keep weathering in scale: Keep scratches and stipple fine, getting finer each stage, and check the scale from arm's length.
texture-in-scale.chunky chips look wrong: Chips that are too chunky look like a toy. Paint finer marks with each stage inside the last.
texture-in-scale.scratches look fake: Too chunky marks look toy like. Keep them fine, with each lighter stage finer and closer to the edge.
texture-in-scale.scale effect on texture: Overscaled texture makes a model look small. Keep marks fine and check them at arm's length.
texture-in-scale.stipple too coarse: Use a fine point, good light and a firm brace, and make each later stage finer than the last.
texture-in-scale.make damage look smaller: Paint each lighter stage finer and inside the last, using a fine point and a firm brace.

touching-up-old-models.old paint job: Refresh it with repairs, touch ups, a wash and new highlights rather than stripping it.
touching-up-old-models.second hand models: Repair loose parts, touch up the main colour, wash to tie old and new paint together, then add fresh highlights.
touching-up-old-models.repaint or strip: Strip only if thick paint has lost the detail. Otherwise paint over it with touch ups, a wash and highlights.
touching-up-old-models.touch up old minis: Touch up with the nearest matching colour, wash to tie old and new paint together, then add fresh highlights.
touching-up-old-models.refresh old models: Reglue loose parts, fill chips, touch up the main colour, wash, then add fresh highlights for contrast.
touching-up-old-models.upgrade an old paint job: List what bothers you, do the biggest fixes first, then wash and add fresh highlights for more contrast.
touching-up-old-models.fix old paint: Reglue loose parts, fill chips and gaps, scrape mould lines, then touch up, wash and rehighlight.
touching-up-old-models.improve my early miniatures: More contrast lifts them most. Touch up, wash to unify, then add fresh highlights.
touching-up-old-models.painted models from a car boot: See: second hand models. Strip only if thick paint hides detail; otherwise repair, touch up, wash and rehighlight.
touching-up-old-models.paint over existing paint: Yes, unless thick paint has lost the detail. Bare spots from scraped mould lines cover in a coat or two.

two-tone-cloaks.two tone cloak: Paint the outside a brighter tone and the lining a deeper one, or a contrasting colour, so the figure stands out.
two-tone-cloaks.cloak lining: Paint the lining darker than the outer face, or in a contrasting colour such as red inside dark green.
two-tone-cloaks.inside of the cloak: Use a deeper tone than the outside, so the darker lining frames the body and stops parts blending together.
two-tone-cloaks.cloak colour: A brighter tone outside and a deeper one on the lining, or a contrasting lining for a more striking look.
two-tone-cloaks.cape: Paint the outer face a brighter tone and the lining and under layers a deeper one.
two-tone-cloaks.what colour inside a cloak: A deeper version of the outside colour, or a contrasting one such as red inside a dark green cloak.
two-tone-cloaks.lining darker than outside: Yes, usually. A darker lining frames the body and keeps parts from blending into each other.
two-tone-cloaks.cloak blends into the body: Paint the lining darker than the outside. It frames the body and separates the parts.
two-tone-cloaks.cape lining: Paint the lining a deeper tone than the outside, or a contrasting colour. A weak paint mixed with a stronger one covers well.
two-tone-cloaks.cloak inner side: Paint the inner side a deeper tone, or a contrasting colour, so the lining frames the figure.

using-filters.filters: A filter is paint thinned about one to nine or ten, brushed or sprayed over a whole surface to tint it without pooling.
using-filters.filter vs wash: A filter is about one part paint to nine or ten thinner and must not pool. A wash is about half and half and pools.
using-filters.how do i use a filter: Seal with satin varnish, then stroke a blotted flat brush lightly top to bottom, or spray light coats. Never flood it.
using-filters.very thin all over tint: That is a filter: paint thinned about one to nine or ten, laid over the whole surface without pooling.
using-filters.unify patchy colours: A very thin filter over the whole area ties patchy colours together. Two thin coats are usually plenty.
using-filters.tone down harsh highlights: Lay a near clear filter over the area. It shifts the tone of the whole surface and softens harsh highlights.
using-filters.filter on a tank: Seal with satin varnish, then brush or spray very thin tint over the whole hull, such as dark brown over green.
using-filters.camo looks disjointed: A thin filter over the camouflage ties the patchy colours together.
using-filters.filter ratio: About one part paint to nine or ten parts thinner.
using-filters.add a dusty cast over everything: Seal with satin varnish, then brush or spray a very thin dark brown filter over the whole surface.

vary-skin-across-a-squad.vary skin tones: Shift each figure slightly warmer, cooler, paler or darker, keeping one shared shade or highlight colour.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.different skin tones in a squad: Give each figure a slightly different tone, and keep a common thread like the same shade colour.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.squad all look the same: Vary skin, hair colour and small details figure to figure, while matching clothing, weapons and bases.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.skin variation: Make one warmer, one cooler, one paler and one darker, with the same final highlight to tie them together.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.squad looks like clones: Shift each figure's skin warmer, cooler, paler or darker, and vary hair colour and small details.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.unit variety: Vary skin tones and small details like hair and war paint, while matching clothing, weapons and bases.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.skin tone variety: Wash the skin on some models and not others, or give a few a grey or paler tone, keeping one shared shade.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.different faces in a unit: Vary the skin tone, hair colour, war paint and touches of red under the eyes and around scars.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.how to make each soldier look different: Shift each one's skin tone slightly and vary hair, war paint and scars, while clothing and bases match.
vary-skin-across-a-squad.unique faces: Give each a slightly different skin tone, hair colour and small details such as war paint or scars.

warm-flush-in-skin.rosy cheeks: Touch very thin red onto the sides of the cheeks and feather the edge out with a damp brush. Keep it subtle.
warm-flush-in-skin.warm flush: Thin red touched onto cheeks, knuckles, joints and ears, feathered out while wet, makes skin look alive.
warm-flush-in-skin.blush on cheeks: Thin a mid red or red and skin mix until see through, touch it on the sides of the cheeks and feather it out.
warm-flush-in-skin.red knuckles: Touch thin red onto the knuckles and into the creases between fingers, feathering the edge while it is wet.
warm-flush-in-skin.warm glaze on skin: Glaze a warm orange flesh mix thinly over skin that has gone dull, and thin bright red into deep recesses.
warm-flush-in-skin.skin looks dull: Glaze a warm orange flesh mix thinly over the whole area, and thin bright red on the sides of the head.
warm-flush-in-skin.skin looks lifeless: Thin warm reds on cheeks, knuckles, joints and ears make painted skin look alive, and a warm glaze rescues dull skin.
warm-flush-in-skin.add colour to skin: Touch thin warm red onto cheeks, knuckles, joints, ears and lips, feathered out, or glaze warm flesh over it.
warm-flush-in-skin.red tint on ears and nose: Touch soft see through red onto the ears and nose and feather it out. On the nose it looks ruddy and cheerful.
warm-flush-in-skin.make skin look alive: Add thin warm reds to cheeks, knuckles, ears and creases, feathered out, and glaze warm flesh over dull skin.

weathered-skin.weathered skin: Use a yellow brown mid tone between a dark red and a peach. It makes skin look thick, rough and older.
weathered-skin.rough tough skin: Base dark red, layer up through yellow brown to peach, and pick out fine detail only on the top highlights.
weathered-skin.old skin: For old, thin skin, dab pale tones loosely and let the warm base show through in spots.
weathered-skin.how do i paint a veteran's face: Dark red base, yellow brown mid tone, peach highlights, with crests of wrinkles lit and folds left dark.
weathered-skin.leathery skin: A yellow brown mid tone between dark red and peach reads thick and rough.
weathered-skin.aged face: Lean the mid tone yellow brown, follow the wrinkles with light on crests, and dab pale tones loosely.
weathered-skin.grizzled face: Dark red, yellow brown and peach, with light on wrinkle crests, folds kept dark and dots on the cheekbones.
weathered-skin.skin looks too young and soft: Pink reads soft and young. Lean the mid tone towards yellow brown instead for tough, older skin.
weathered-skin.yellow brown skin tone: Yellow brown makes skin look thick, rough and older, while a pink mid tone reads soft and young.
weathered-skin.battle hardened warrior skin: Dark red base, a yellow brown mid tone and peach highlights, with fine detail on the nose, knuckles and scars.

wet-blending-contrast-paints.wet blend contrast: Paint the first one coat paint halfway, then the second from the other end, brushing back and forth where they meet.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.blending contrast paints: Thin them, paint each from opposite ends and brush back and forth where they meet. They often bleed together.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.contrast gradient: Over a pale or zenithal primer, paint one colour halfway, the next from the other end, and blend the join wet.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.wet blending speed paints: See: one coat paints, which dry slowly. This entry paints two from opposite ends and blends the join wet.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.blend two one coat paints: Paint one halfway, rinse, paint the other from the opposite end, and brush back and forth where they meet.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.how do i blend contrast on the model: Work from light into dark, thin strong colours, and brush back and forth where the two meet while wet.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.same gradient across a batch: Go darker at the feet and brighter towards the head on every model, then glaze for depth once dry.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.fast gradient on a cloak: Paint one colour from the hem, the other from the top, and brush back and forth where they meet.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.contrast fade on a cloak: Use clear medium as the second colour to fade the paint out into the colour below.
wet-blending-contrast-paints.blend contrast over zenithal: Zenithal prime keeps colours bright. Blend two thinned one coat paints wet from opposite ends of the area.

when-washes-work.when to use a wash: Use a wash on sharp, deep detail like fur, hair, chainmail and texture, over mid tone colours.
when-washes-work.wash on cloak: Large smooth areas like cloaks tend to collect tide marks and blotches. Use layers or glazes instead.
when-washes-work.wash fails: Washes struggle on big smooth areas, very pale or dark bases, and cannot fix the wrong base colour.
when-washes-work.wash streaks: On layer printed scenery, washes run along the ridges and stain in stripes. Spray thinned paint instead.
when-washes-work.wash looks bad: Washes struggle on big smooth areas and very pale or very dark colours. Repaint the wrong base colour.
when-washes-work.wash on skin: Bare skin tends to collect tide marks and blotches, so layers or glazes usually work better.
when-washes-work.wash on 3d print: Washes run along print ridges and stain in stripes. Airbrush thinned one coat paint into the shadows instead.
when-washes-work.wash on pale colour: Even a weak wash stains pale colours. Use an oil wash or a fine line of thinned paint in the recesses instead.
when-washes-work.wash tide marks on big areas: Large smooth areas collect tide marks. Shade them with layers or glazes rather than a wash.
when-washes-work.should i wash everything: No. Washes suit deep detail over mid tones and darken every recess equally, so they rarely suffice alone.

worn-metal-edges.worn metal edges: Dab a broken line of bright silver along edges, rivets and pits over a dull, darkened metal base.
worn-metal-edges.chipped metal: Over dull dark metal, dab broken bright silver along edges in short strokes, gaps and dots.
worn-metal-edges.how do i paint worn metal: Base dull, run thinned black into recesses, then dab broken bright silver along edges, rivets and pits.
worn-metal-edges.scratched metal: Dull metal base, then broken bright silver marks on edges, rivets and the rims of pits, mostly small.
worn-metal-edges.battered armour: Dab broken bright silver on the edges and corners that stick out, mostly as small chips.
worn-metal-edges.bare metal showing through: Paint fine silver lines along dark worn edges of painted armour to read as paint scraped to bare metal.
worn-metal-edges.silver edges: Dab, do not line: short strokes, gaps and dots of bright silver along the edges over dull metal.
worn-metal-edges.worn edges: Dab short strokes and dots of bright silver along edges instead of a clean line, mostly small.
worn-metal-edges.nicked metal: Dab short silver strokes and dots on edges, rivets and pits, and add a few freehand nicks.
worn-metal-edges.make metal look old and battered: Dab broken bright silver on edges and rivets over dull metal, then a thin rusty brown glaze for grime.

cobblestone-streets.cobble base: Press stone shapes into a thin layer of putty, push the gaps down so each stone stands proud, then paint cool grey with brown washed into the gaps.
cobblestone-streets.how to make cobblestones on a base: Spread thin putty, press in stone shapes or roll a cobble texture roller over it, deepen the gaps with a damp brush, trim, cure and paint.
cobblestone-streets.city street base for my models: Use putty cobbles with dirt and small debris in the gaps, painted a varied cool grey with brown grime and a few khaki stone edges.
cobblestone-streets.cobbled road with putty: Spread a thin layer of putty and press in stone shapes, pushing the gaps down with a damp brush or shaper so each stone stands proud.
cobblestone-streets.medieval town ground for a base: Putty cobbles with mud, bones, pots or scrap wood in the gaps, then grey stones, brown grime and tufts and flowers hiding messy patches.
cobblestone-streets.stone street with rubbish in the cracks: Scatter dirt and small debris such as bones, pots or scrap wood into the gaps, seal with thin super glue and blot the excess straight away.
cobblestone-streets.cobblestones look flat, how do i make th: Push the gaps deeper so each stone stands proud, vary the grey per stone, run brown into the gaps and edge a few stones in grey khaki.
cobblestone-streets.urban fantasy basing: See: cobblestone streets, a putty town street with mud and debris in the gaps, which suits a city setting.
cobblestone-streets.texture roller for cobbles: Roll the cobble texture roller across the putty in one even pass, then push the gaps down with a damp brush so the stones stand proud.
cobblestone-streets.cobblestone basing tutorial: Press putty cobbles, cure and sand a few flat, add dirt and debris with super glue, then paint grey, wash brown and edge a few stones khaki.

dungeon-flagstones.dungeon floor base: Paint sculpted flagstones dark grey, wash brown and green together for damp moss, drybrush light grey then pale bone, and finish matt.
dungeon-flagstones.how do i paint stone flags for indoor ba: Prime grey, paint the stones dark grey, mix brown and green washes on them, then drybrush light grey and a dusting of pale bone.
dungeon-flagstones.damp dark stone floor: Wash brown and green at the same time, swapping at random so they mix into a damp, mossy look over dark grey stone.
dungeon-flagstones.flagstone base for a dungeon crawler: Dark grey flags with mixed brown and green washes, a light grey and pale bone drybrush, a matt black rim and matt varnish.
dungeon-flagstones.make floor tiles look old and grimy: Brush thinned earth texture or fine sand over the stones so it settles in the joints, then wash brown and green and drybrush lightly.
dungeon-flagstones.dirt in the gaps between stones: Brush thinned earth texture paint or fine sand over the stones so it settles into the gaps, then wash and drybrush it.
dungeon-flagstones.dark grey stone tiles base: Base them dark grey, mix brown and green washes on top, then drybrush light grey and a dusting of pale bone, with a matt black rim.
dungeon-flagstones.why do my floor tiles all look the same: Tint a few single slabs a little warmer or cooler than the rest, and swap between brown and green washes at random.
dungeon-flagstones.crypt floor: See: dungeon flagstones, dark damp stone with brown and green washes, which suits crypt and indoor floors.
dungeon-flagstones.dungeon tiles painting: Dark grey base, brown and green washes mixed on the stone, a light grey drybrush, pale bone dusting, then matt varnish.

natural-tufts.tufts look stuck on: Tint bright tufts with a muted paint, cut flat edges to sit against rocks, push them into cracks, and wash brown into the roots.
natural-tufts.grass tufts look plastic: Tint them on the backing sheet with a one coat paint in muted green or straw, then wash the roots brown and drybrush the tips pale.
natural-tufts.how to make static grass tufts look real: Tint, trim stray fibres, glue them deep into cracks and corners, then wash the roots brown and blend earth pigment round them.
natural-tufts.tufts too bright green: Tint them on their backing sheet with a one coat paint in a muted green or straw and let them dry before use.
natural-tufts.tint grass tufts: Paint bright, plastic looking tufts on their backing sheet with a one coat paint in a muted green or straw.
natural-tufts.tuft against a rock: Cut the tuft in half from the side so its flat edge sits tight against the rock, then push it hard into the crack.
natural-tufts.cutting tufts in half: Cutting a tuft in half from the side gives a flat edge that sits snugly against rocks and walls.
natural-tufts.grass clumps look fake on bases: Tint them muted, set them in cracks and dips, poke brown wash into the roots and stroke pale straw over the tips.
natural-tufts.make tufts look like they grow: Push them into cracks and dips, wash the roots brown, and flow watery earth pigment round them so they look grown in.
natural-tufts.where to put tufts on a base: Push tufts into cracks, corners and dips where water would gather, tallest in shelter, a few tiny ones in the open.

sand-and-rocks.simple sand base: Glue a few slate pieces, sand round them with white glue, stain warm brown, then drybrush sand, grey on rocks and pale bone over all.
sand-and-rocks.quick basing for a whole army: Slate rocks and sand on white glue, a thin warm brown stain, a few drybrushes, then a tuft or two: quick enough for a whole army.
sand-and-rocks.sand and rocks on bases: Glue two to four slate pieces of mixed sizes, brush white glue round them, dip in sand, then stain and drybrush.
sand-and-rocks.how do i base lots of models fast: Use slate and sand with white glue, a thin warm stain over everything, then quick drybrushes for sand, rocks and a pale tie in.
sand-and-rocks.easy desert base: Warm sand with a few cool grey slate rocks, stained brown and drybrushed sand, grey and pale bone, plus a tuft or two.
sand-and-rocks.slate rocks on a base: Glue two to four slate pieces of different sizes on each base, with one stray rock placed away from the cluster.
sand-and-rocks.how to glue sand on bases: Brush white glue out from the centre, dip the base in sand, tap off the extra, and let it dry naturally.
sand-and-rocks.basic beginner basing: Slate and sand on white glue, a thin brown stain, drybrush sand, grey and pale bone, a khaki brown rim and a tuft.
sand-and-rocks.sand keeps falling off my base: Drip thinned white glue over the loose sand to lock it, let it dry naturally, and sweep off dust with a soft brush before priming.
sand-and-rocks.rocks and tufts on round bases: Glue slate in a small cluster with one stray rock, sand the rest, then drybrush the rocks grey and add a tuft or two with white glue.

swamp-and-bog.swamp base: Dark mud paste with moss and a twig log, a murky pond with a dark centre, green wash for algae and a gloss finish over the wet areas.
swamp-and-bog.how to make a muddy bog base: Dab on thick dark mud paste, press in moss and a twig while wet, run green wash in for algae, then gloss the low ground.
swamp-and-bog.murky water on a base: Leave a hollow, paint its bed dark in the middle fading to lighter green at the shore, then fill with clear gloss gel or water effect.
swamp-and-bog.wet mud look: Add gloss wet effect gel over the matt washed mud; the gloss is what makes it read as boggy.
swamp-and-bog.mossy log and pond base: Press a real twig and moss pads into wet mud paste, leave a hollow for a pond with a dark centre, then gloss the pond.
swamp-and-bog.make mud look wet and glossy: Run green wash into dark mud for algae, then put clear gloss gel over it and the low ground so it looks wet.
swamp-and-bog.marsh basing ideas: Dark mud paste, a murky pond, a twig log, hanging moss from cotton wool, and gloss on the low ground.
swamp-and-bog.boggy ground for a frog model: See: swamp and bog, dark wet mud with a murky pond and moss, which suits a frog model.
swamp-and-bog.hanging moss on bases: Soak cotton wool in one part glue to three of water, tease into strands on plastic, drape over a log and wash dark green.
swamp-and-bog.green stagnant pond: Paint the pond bed dark green in the middle blending to grass green at the edge, a near black glaze in the deepest part, then gloss.

wooden-plank-floors.wooden floor base: Glue wooden strips across the base, harden with thin super glue, scratch in grain and nail holes, then paint and wash each plank differently.
wooden-plank-floors.ship deck base: Glue wooden strips in a few widths, score the grain, add nail holes, then vary browns and washes per plank and wipe the tops back.
wooden-plank-floors.coffee stirrer planks: Any thin wooden strips work: glue them across the base, soak with thin super glue, trim, then scratch grain and nail holes.
wooden-plank-floors.boardwalk base: Glue wooden strips side by side with small gaps, harden and trim them, then paint weathered brown and drybrush pale grey along the grain.
wooden-plank-floors.how to make planks on a base: Glue wooden strips across the base in a few widths, soak with thin super glue, trim flush, scratch the grain and prime black.
wooden-plank-floors.broken floorboards: Leave a snapped board or small gaps when gluing the strips down, and prime black so the gaps stay dark.
wooden-plank-floors.weathered wood planks for bases: Score the grain and press nail holes, vary the brown per plank, wash with different washes, wipe the tops back and drybrush pale grey.
wooden-plank-floors.pirate ship deck on base: See: wooden plank floors, weathered planks that suit ship decks, floors and walkways.
wooden-plank-floors.walkway made of wood strips: Glue wood strips across the base in a few widths, soak with thin super glue, trim flush, then scratch the grain and paint.
wooden-plank-floors.balsa wood floor tiles: Glue balsa strips in a few widths, harden with thin super glue, trim, gouge the grain, then prime black and paint varied browns.

black-feathers.black feathers: Base black, drybrush dark grey fairly heavily, flick cool blue grey on the sharpest edges, then tie it together with a thin black glaze.
black-feathers.how do i paint black wings: Base black, heavy dark grey drybrush, a very light cool blue grey drybrush on the sharpest feather edges, then a thinned black glaze.
black-feathers.dark feathers drybrush: Drybrush dark grey fairly heavily over a black base with no wash first, then a very light blue grey on the sharpest edges only.
black-feathers.raven wings look flat: Drybrush dark grey over black, catch the sharpest feather edges in a light blue grey, then glaze thinned black to pull the steps together.
black-feathers.crow feathers paint recipe: Black base, dark grey drybrush, a hint of cool blue grey on the edges, and a thinned black glaze to finish.
black-feathers.how to highlight black feathers: Drybrush dark grey over black, then a very light cool blue grey on only the sharpest feather edges for a hint of colour.
black-feathers.feathered cloak in black: Base black, drybrush dark grey, touch the sharpest edges with cool blue grey, then a thin black glaze to unify it.
black-feathers.dry brushing feathers grey: Go fairly heavy with dark grey over a black base, no wash needed first, then very lightly add blue grey to the sharpest edges.
black-feathers.black bird wings on a model: Base black, drybrush dark grey and then a light cool blue grey on the edges, and finish with a thinned black glaze.
black-feathers.black glaze over feathers: Thin a black one coat paint with medium and glaze it over the drybrushed greys to pull the steps together.

blue-lightning.blue lightning effect: Glaze deep sea blue in rough forking lines, a thinner bright blue line inside, pale icy blue at the centres, then white dots at the brightest points.
blue-lightning.electric arcs on a sword: Glaze rough forking lines in deep blue along the metal, add a bright blue line inside, icy blue at the forks, and white dots on top.
blue-lightning.crackling energy on metal: Thin deep blue glazes around the source and along forking lines, building through bright blue and icy blue to a few white dots.
blue-lightning.how do i paint electricity: Paint rough forking lines in thin deep blue glazes, then a thinner bright blue inside, pale icy blue where forks meet, and white dots.
blue-lightning.lightning on a power weapon: Glaze deep blue forks out from the source, a brighter blue line inside, pale icy blue cores, and white strokes at the brightest points.
blue-lightning.glowing blue sparks: Build thin glazes from deep blue to bright mid blue to pale icy blue, then dot white at the brightest points.
blue-lightning.energy weapon effect: See: blue lightning, glazed arcs from deep blue edges to white hot cores, which works as an energy effect on metal.
blue-lightning.blue lightening: Deep blue glazes along forking lines, a bright blue line inside, icy blue at the centres, then a few white dots and strokes.
blue-lightning.white hot core lightning: Keep pale icy blue only at the centres where forks meet and at the source, then add white dots and short strokes at the brightest points.
blue-lightning.electrified blade: Glaze forking lines of deep sea blue over the blade, then bright blue, icy blue cores and a few white dots near the source.

bright-steel-armour.shiny silver armour: Base a very dark silver, drybrush mid steel, wash soft black, then drybrush a little pure silver across the edges.
bright-steel-armour.bright steel knights: Dark silver base, mid steel drybrush, a thin soft black wash, then a bright silver drybrush across the edges at a right angle.
bright-steel-armour.clean metal armour: Start from a dark silver, drybrush mid steel, wash soft black into details, then a light bright silver drybrush on the edges.
bright-steel-armour.how to paint silver armour quickly: Base silver mixed with black or use a silver spray primer, drybrush mid steel, wash soft black, then drybrush bright silver.
bright-steel-armour.make silver armor pop: The pop comes from the contrast: a very dark silver base, a soft black wash, then a little pure silver drybrushed across the edges.
bright-steel-armour.polished plate armour: Very dark silver base, mid steel drybrush, a soft black wash, then very little bright silver brushed across the edges.
bright-steel-armour.silver drybrush on armour: Drybrush mid steel top down over a dark silver base, then after a black wash use very little pure silver across the edges.
bright-steel-armour.metal armour looks dull: Start darker: a silver mixed with black base, then drybrush lighter steel and finish with pure silver on the edges.
bright-steel-armour.knight armour recipe: Dark silver base, mid steel drybrush, soft black wash, then a little bright silver across the edges.
bright-steel-armour.bright silver over dark base: Use very little pure silver, brushed across the edges at a right angle, over a very dark silver base and black wash.

dark-blue-armour.dark blue armour: Base a deep rich blue, wash black, layer the blue back on flat panels, then edge mid blue and flick pale grey blue on the sharpest corners.
dark-blue-armour.deep navy armor recipe: Deep blue base, black wash, the blue layered back on the panels, mid blue edges and pale grey blue on the sharpest corners.
dark-blue-armour.how to paint dark blue armour: Base two coats of deep blue over mid grey primer, wash black all over, layer the blue back, then edge in mid and pale grey blue.
dark-blue-armour.blue armour looks too black after wash: Layer the deep blue back onto the flat panels after the black wash, leaving the black only in the recesses.
dark-blue-armour.rich blue power armour: Deep rich blue base, black wash, blue layered back on the panels, then mid blue and pale grey blue edge highlights.
dark-blue-armour.navy blue knight: Deep blue base, black wash, layer the blue back on flat areas, then edge with mid blue and a pale grey blue on corners.
dark-blue-armour.edge highlight dark blue: Edge most edges in mid blue with the side of the brush, then flick thinned pale grey blue onto the sharpest corners only.
dark-blue-armour.midnight blue armour: Base deep rich blue, wash black, layer the blue back on the panels, and edge in mid blue then pale grey blue.
dark-blue-armour.washed blue armour layered back: Wash black all over the deep blue, then layer the blue back on the flat panels before edging in two lighter blues.
dark-blue-armour.how do i keep dark blue from going dull: Layer the blue back over the black wash on the flat panels, then edge mid blue and a pale grey blue on the sharpest corners.

drab-greatcoat.greatcoat: Base mid blue grey, wash dark brown, layer a lighter blue grey on raised folds, then edge hems and crease tops in a pale blue grey.
drab-greatcoat.how do i paint a wool coat: Base a muted colour, wash dark brown, layer lighter tones on raised folds only, then edge hems and crease tops in a warm pale tone.
drab-greatcoat.drab blue grey coat: Two coats of mid blue grey over grey primer, a dark brown wash, a lighter blue grey on folds, and pale blue grey on the hems.
drab-greatcoat.military trench coat: See: drab wool greatcoat, a muted field coat in blue grey or olive brown with crisp folds and hems.
drab-greatcoat.soldier coat brown: Base a drab olive brown, wash dark brown, layer a lighter tone on raised folds, and edge hems and crease tops in a warm pale tone.
drab-greatcoat.old army uniform coat: See: drab wool greatcoat, a muted blue grey or olive brown field coat with crisp folds and hems.
drab-greatcoat.muted coat colours: Drab blue grey or olive brown, washed dark brown, with lighter folds and a warm pale edge rather than white.
drab-greatcoat.long coat folds: Layer a lighter tone on the raised folds only, skipping the creases, then catch the crease tops with the brush tip.
drab-greatcoat.infantry greatcoat: Base mid blue grey or drab olive brown, wash dark brown, layer lighter on the folds and edge hems and creases in a pale tone.
drab-greatcoat.paint wool cloth: Base a muted mid tone, wash dark brown, layer the raised folds lighter and edge the hems with the side of the brush.

glowing-water.glowing water: Base a strong blue over white, edge light blue on edges and droplet tips, stipple near white bubbles, then gloss varnish.
glowing-water.magic water effect: Strong blue over a white base, light blue on edges and droplet tips, loose near white dots for reflections, and gloss on top.
glowing-water.bright blue water: Paint a strong blue over white so it stays intense, highlight light blue, stipple near white dots and finish with clear gloss.
glowing-water.glowing blue liquid: Two coats of strong blue over a white base, light blue edges, near white bubble dots, then a gloss varnish.
glowing-water.water elemental: See: glowing magic water, a strong blue over white with bright spots, which suits a water elemental.
glowing-water.enchanted pool: Strong blue over a white base, light blue on the edges, near white dots for reflections, and a gloss coat.
glowing-water.how to make water look lit up: Paint over white so the blue stays intense, add light blue edges and near white dots of different sizes, then gloss it.
glowing-water.glowing blue droplets: Base strong blue over white, edge the droplet tips in light blue with off white, then gloss varnish.
glowing-water.spell water splash: Strong blue over white, light blue on small edges and droplet tips, near white bubble dots, then clear gloss.
glowing-water.intense blue over white: A white base keeps the strong blue intense; add light blue edges, near white dots and a gloss finish.

grey-hide.grey skin on a beast: Drybrush mid grey over a dark undercoat, wash brown with a little water, drybrush light warm grey on the folds, then dusty bone on the legs.
grey-hide.how to paint elephant skin: Drybrush mid grey over a dark undercoat, wash brown, light warm grey on the fold tops, and dusty bone around the lower legs.
grey-hide.rhino hide paint: Mid grey drybrush, thinned brown wash, light warm grey drybrush on the folds, then dusty bone flicked on the lower legs.
grey-hide.thick animal skin grey: Drybrush mid grey over dark, wash brown so it settles in the folds, then light warm grey on the wrinkle tops.
grey-hide.dusty legs on a monster: Flick a dusty bone drybrush around the feet and lower legs as dust.
grey-hide.grey textured skin recipe: Two mid grey drybrushes over a dark undercoat, a brown wash, light warm grey on the folds, and dusty bone on the lower legs.
grey-hide.big beast hide looks blotchy: Add a little water to the brown wash so it settles into the folds without blotches.
grey-hide.wash grey skin without blotches: Thin the brown wash with a little water and take it all over, so it settles in the folds without blotches.
grey-hide.mammoth hide: Drybrush mid grey over dark, wash brown, light warm grey on the fold tops, and dusty bone on the legs and tusks.
grey-hide.grey troll skin: Mid grey drybrush over a dark undercoat, a thinned brown wash, then a light warm grey drybrush on the wrinkles.

jade-gem.jade gem: Base deep jade, wash black on the gem, layer light jade on the lower left, then one small white dot in the upper right.
jade-gem.green gem: Deep jade base, black wash, lighter jade on the lower left half, and a single white dot upper right.
jade-gem.how to paint a green gemstone: Fill it deep jade, wash black, layer lighter jade toward the lower left corner, then dot white in the upper right.
jade-gem.emerald on a sword hilt: Deep jade base, black wash, light jade layered on the lower left, and a small white dot in the upper right.
jade-gem.green jewel: Deep jade, a black wash, light jade on the lower left half, then one white dot in the upper right corner.
jade-gem.gem glow from below: Layer a light jade on the lower left half, then a lighter jade nearer that corner, opposite the white dot.
jade-gem.make a gem look shiny: One small white dot in the upper right corner, opposite the lighter lower glow.
jade-gem.paint gems green: Base deep jade, wash black, layer light jade low on one side and add a white dot on the opposite corner.
jade-gem.green stone in an amulet: Deep jade base, black wash kept on the gem, light jade on the lower left, white dot upper right.
jade-gem.jade jewel: Fill with deep jade, wash black, layer two light jades toward the lower left, and add one white dot upper right.

olive-skin.olive skin: Drybrush warm flesh over a peach undercoat, coat a one coat ochre all over, layer light amber skin on raised areas, then glaze light flesh.
olive-skin.mediterranean skin tone: Use an ochre in place of the usual flesh: warm flesh drybrush, ochre over it, light amber on the raised areas, then a light flesh glaze.
olive-skin.tanned skin: Warm flesh drybrush over peach, an ochre coat all over, a light amber layer on raised areas, and a thin light flesh glaze.
olive-skin.ochre skin: Use an ochre one coat paint over a warm flesh drybrush, layer light amber on top, then glaze light flesh to pull it back towards skin.
olive-skin.warm skin recipe: Warm flesh drybrush over a peach undercoat, an ochre coat, light amber on the raised areas, then a light flesh glaze.
olive-skin.darker than pale but not dark skin: For an olive tone, coat ochre over a warm flesh drybrush, layer light amber on raised areas, then glaze light flesh.
olive-skin.skin looks too yellow: It looks too yellow at first, which is fine: a light flesh glaze pulls it back towards skin while keeping the olive tone.
olive-skin.middle eastern skin tone: For an olive tone, drybrush warm flesh over peach, coat ochre, layer light amber on raised areas, then glaze light flesh.
olive-skin.olive complexion: Warm flesh drybrush, a one coat ochre over it, light amber on the raised areas, then a thin light flesh glaze.
olive-skin.sun tanned flesh: Drybrush warm flesh over peach, coat ochre all over, layer light amber on the raised areas, and glaze light flesh to finish.

pale-corpse-skin.pale dead skin: Base greyish pale flesh, wash purple into the recesses, layer near white flesh on the high points, then a very thin soft red glaze.
pale-corpse-skin.zombie skin recipe: Greyish pale flesh base, purple or dark blue wash in the recesses, near white flesh on the high points, and a faint red glaze round the eyes.
pale-corpse-skin.corpse flesh: Base a light flesh with grey mixed in, wash purple into the recesses, then build up near white flesh on cheekbones, brow and nose.
pale-corpse-skin.vampire skin: Greyish pale flesh, purple recesses, near white flesh on the high points, and a very thin soft red round the eyes, nose and lips.
pale-corpse-skin.how do i paint undead skin: Base a greyed pale flesh, wash purple in the recesses, layer up near white flesh, then glaze faint red so it still looks alive.
pale-corpse-skin.pale skin with purple shadows: Base greyish pale flesh, then wash purple into the recesses only, where it reads as lavender.
pale-corpse-skin.cold pale flesh: Base a light flesh drained with grey, wash the recesses purple or dark blue, and layer near white flesh on the high points.
pale-corpse-skin.lavender recesses on skin: Keep a thinned purple wash in the recesses only over a greyish pale flesh base, where it reads as lavender.
pale-corpse-skin.ghoulish skin tone: Greyish pale flesh with purple recesses, near white highlights on the face, and a very faint red flush around the eyes.
pale-corpse-skin.sickly pale face: Mix grey into a light flesh for the base, wash purple in the recesses, and build near white on cheekbones, brow, nose and lips.

plum-red-rope.plum rope: Base plum red from dark purple and deep red, wash black in the recesses, layer a lighter red, then edge pale pink on the raised twists.
plum-red-rope.dark red cord: Mix dark purple with deep red, wash black into the recesses, layer lighter with bone or pale yellow, then pale pink on the raised twists.
plum-red-rope.tassels colour: See: plum red rope, a deep plum red that suits rope, cord and tassels.
plum-red-rope.deep red rope: Plum red base, thinned black wash in the recesses, a lighter red layer, and pale pink on the raised twists.
plum-red-rope.purple red cord: Mix dark purple and deep red, wash thinned black into the recesses, then lighten with pale yellow or bone stage by stage.
plum-red-rope.how do i paint tassels: Base plum red, wash thinned black in the recesses, layer a lighter red, then edge the raised parts in pale pink.
plum-red-rope.wine red rope: Plum red base from dark purple and deep red, black wash, lighter red layer, and pale pink on the raised twists.
plum-red-rope.maroon cord: Base dark purple mixed with deep red, wash black, layer lighter red and edge pale pink on the twists.
plum-red-rope.rope and tassel colour: See: plum red rope, a deep plum red for rope, cord and tassels.
plum-red-rope.dark red belt cord: Base plum red, wash thinned black, layer a lighter red, then edge the raised parts pale pink.

red-hot-metal.red hot metal: Paint the hottest area solid white, glaze very thin bright red over it, add orange glazes at the core, then a pale yellow line at the very ends.
red-hot-metal.glowing hot blade: Layer the hot end white until opaque, glaze thin bright red towards the tip, orange at the core, and edge the ends pale yellow.
red-hot-metal.how to make a gun barrel look overheated: Paint the barrel end white until opaque, glaze thin bright red pulled to the tip, then orange near the core and a fine pale yellow edge.
red-hot-metal.molten metal effect: Opaque white on the hottest area, very thin bright red glazes, orange towards the tips and core, then a pale yellow edge.
red-hot-metal.forge hot sword: Solid white on the hot area, thin bright red glazes over it, orange near the tip, a pale yellow edge, and black chunks for crust.
red-hot-metal.glowing coils on a weapon: Paint the coils white until opaque, then glaze very thin red and orange over them towards the brightest point.
red-hot-metal.white hot core fading to red: Paint the core opaque white, glaze thin bright red pulled towards it, then orange near the core and pale yellow on the very ends.
red-hot-metal.metal glowing orange from heat: Lay down opaque white where it is hottest, then thin bright red glazes and orange glazes kept towards the core.
red-hot-metal.heat glow on exhaust pipes: Paint the hottest area white, then glaze thin bright red and orange over it, with a pale yellow line on the very ends.
red-hot-metal.hot metal doesnt look like it glows: Paint the hottest area white until opaque first, so the red and orange glazes on top can glow.

toxic-green-glow.toxic green glow: Paint the source and drybrush mid green outwards, glaze thin mid green over the lit area, drybrush yellow green near it, then pale green at the centre.
toxic-green-glow.radioactive glow effect: Mid green drybrush out from the source, a thin mid green glaze, yellow green on nearby edges and a pale green glaze in the centre.
toxic-green-glow.how to paint glowing green: Drybrush mid green outwards from the source, tint with a thin green glaze, add yellow green on edges near it, then pale green at the centre.
toxic-green-glow.sickly green light: Build from mid green up to yellow green: drybrush, glaze about one part paint to five water, drybrush lighter, then pale green at the core.
toxic-green-glow.glowing green crystals: Paint the crystals as the source, drybrush mid green outwards, glaze thin green, and finish yellow green and pale green at the centre.
toxic-green-glow.green glow drybrush: Drybrush mid green outwards over raised areas, then a lighter yellow green drybrush on edges near the source only.
toxic-green-glow.slime glow: See: toxic green glow, a sickly green built from mid green up to yellow green.
toxic-green-glow.make green look like it glows: Keep it brightest at the source: yellow green on nearby edges and a thin pale green in the centre, over mid green.
toxic-green-glow.nuclear green: See: toxic green glow, a sickly mid green built up to yellow green at the source.
toxic-green-glow.glowing green vials: Paint the vial as the source, drybrush and glaze mid green outward, then yellow green near it and a pale green glaze at the centre.

weathered-grey-wood.grey wood: Thin light grey brown over a zenithal undercoat, a mid brown glaze on a few planks only, then pale grey on the upward facing parts.
weathered-grey-wood.old weathered wood: Base thin light grey brown, glaze mid brown on a few planks so boards vary, then layer pale grey on upward facing parts only.
weathered-grey-wood.sun bleached planks: Thin light grey brown base, a mid brown glaze on some planks, and pale grey with a little wood colour on the tops.
weathered-grey-wood.driftwood: See: weathered grey wood, a sun bleached grey kept light with glazes and top only highlights.
weathered-grey-wood.how to paint aged wood: Base light grey brown over a zenithal undercoat, glaze a few planks mid brown, then pale grey on the upward facing parts.
weathered-grey-wood.grey wooden fence: Light grey brown base, a thin mid brown glaze on a few boards so they vary, then pale grey on the tops.
weathered-grey-wood.weathered barrels: Base light grey brown, glaze some staves mid brown, then pale grey on the upward facing parts only.
weathered-grey-wood.silvery old timber: Keep it light: thin light grey brown, a few boards glazed mid brown, then pale grey with a little wood colour on top.
weathered-grey-wood.wood looks too brown: Use a light grey brown base and keep the brown glaze to a few planks only, then pale grey on the upward facing parts.
weathered-grey-wood.old boards on a base: Thin light grey brown over a zenithal undercoat, mid brown glaze on a few boards, pale grey on the tops.

yellow-over-warm-undercoat.yellow over pink undercoat: Prime hot pink, dust white from above, coat a thinned yellow one coat paint, then edge pale cream: the shadows turn warm orange.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.yellow shadows go green and muddy: Prime pink or orange instead, so a thinned yellow coat over it shades to warm orange in the recesses rather than green.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.warm orange shadows on yellow: Prime hot pink, dust white from above to leave pink in the recesses, then coat a thinned bright yellow over everything.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.yellow over orange: An orange undercoat also works and gives softer warm shadows under a thinned yellow coat than pink.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.how do i paint yellow: Prime hot pink, dust white from above, coat a yellow one coat paint or ink thinned half and half, then pale cream edges.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.yellow wont cover: Thin a yellow one coat paint or ink about half and half over a pink undercoat dusted with white from above.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.bright yellow armour: Prime hot pink, dust white from above, two coats of thinned bright yellow, then pale cream on the sharpest edges.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.best undercoat for yellow: A hot pink or orange undercoat dusted with white from above, so the shadows under the yellow turn warm orange.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.yellow looks dirty when shaded: Prime pink or orange so the shading under yellow reads warm orange rather than dirty.
yellow-over-warm-undercoat.yello armour over pink: Prime hot pink, dust white from above, coat thinned bright yellow twice, then edge the sharpest edges pale cream.

airbrush-highlights.airbrush highlights: Spray a shadow tone over everything, then each lighter tone into a smaller area where light hits, and sharpen the brightest spots by brush.
airbrush-highlights.how do i highlight with an airbrush: Mix shadow, mid and light tones, spray the shadow solid, then the mid tone from above towards panel centres, and the light tone smaller still.
airbrush-highlights.spraying lighter tones: Spray each lighter tone into a smaller area on the upper surfaces, stopping earlier than feels natural so the darker ring stays visible.
airbrush-highlights.airbrush shading: Spray the dark tone solid into the recesses first, then lighter tones from above; if you lose the shadows, spray the shadow mix back from below.
airbrush-highlights.keep army colours consistent airbrush: Mix the shadow, mid and light tones before you start and label them or keep leftovers in small lidded jars so a whole army matches.
airbrush-highlights.airbrushing light and shadow: Spray dark everywhere, a mid tone from above towards panel centres, then a light tone only on the top surfaces at lower pressure.
airbrush-highlights.airbrush gradient on armour: Spray the mid tone towards panel centres leaving a dark ring at the edges, then the light tone on top; a straight edged card gives crisp panel highlights.
airbrush-highlights.air brush highlighting: Lay the shadow tone over everything, spray each lighter tone into a smaller area from above, then sharpen the brightest spots by brush.
